review_title: Makes for tasty, comforting sipping broth, 8 grams collagen (7 grams protein) per serving
review_text:
I really like this! I have the flavored (turmeric) option, and it is better than expected. When I see powdered "bone broth", I basically expect zero flavor (which is fine as it is the collagen I am after), but this flavored variety isn't just a "flavored" plain powder, it actually tastes like broth. And not just turmeric, but an interesting "sipping broth" with depth of flavor. Not too salty, but it does have 210 mg per serving. I am enjoying it a lot during these extra cold winter days. Take a look at the ingredient list in their product picture, and you will see that it has a soup broth tasting vibe to it.

NOTE ON COLLAGEN. The "beef broth propriety blend" states that is has 12.9 grams. Within this blend there is collagen. You may be wondering how much exactly. Little trick: collagen and protein have a near 1:1 ratio. The protein has to be listed separately on a nutrition label. This label says it has 7 grams of protein per serving, SO given this, you will know that there is 7-8 grams of collagen per serving.

The directions say to use 1 scoop in hot or warm water, but not how much water. I assumed 8 ounces, and I think that is accurate. I used two scoops in a 16 ounce mason jar (maybe filled 14 ounces of water), and that tasted very nice. I drank it as is, but it would work great with some added protein, noodles, veggies, etc added in. Could add to other broth, or whatever.

4.5 stars, but making it 5 because I like it more than 4 (and we cant do half stars). ALSO, I just added another tub to my cart so that says somethinbg. The current 30% coupon makes it more reasonably priced than the $29 price tag

review_text:

So this size in comparison to most is a larger serving. I usually use about 3/4 of scoop full, or do two half servings through day.

As for the container being half empty? Products are sold based on weight, not volume. When the powder settles it is half full. When I shake it up, it is three quarters full. While it could be a smaller container, it isn't unreasonable. Also, it comes with a scoop, which takes up room. Why down rate. you are not getting less product (aiming this at review who said this is a scam).

review_text: CAFE LATTE  Tried this for the first time yesterday, and won't be purchasing again.  There are several issues.  First the flavor.  I mixed it with milk and as I raise my glass I smelled what smelled like burning rubber.  So, I got another glass and tried again.  Still smelled like burning rubber.  It did NOT taste like burning rubber, it was virtually tasteless, just sweet.  Second the labeling is very misleading.  To begin with I ordered cafe latte, but no where on the label does it say what flavor it is.  The only reason I know it was the cafe latte flavor was the color being tan and a recipe they had on the side saying morning mocha bowl, calling for a scoop of cafe latte protein mix.  Then the nutrition information label says serving size 2 scoops, but no directions as to mixing or amounts.  There is a picture next to the nutrition label saying  "Easy to enjoy" saying "it only takes 6-8oz of water and 1 serving of powder to make a shake."  Two scoops of powder is the equivalent of 1/3 cup, 6 oz of water is 3/4 cup, which to me, seems like a lot of powder for a small serving.  Since when is 6 oz a serving of any liquid?  Be that as it may, it was very disappointing, especially since "essence of burning rubber" is not one of my favorite flavors.

* Using a blender bottle and milk produces a very airy/foamy drink. So foamy that I likely won't use this won't be using this powder with a blender bottle going forward. My wife says not using milk helps with this in general but I hate not using milk with protein powder while she's OK with it.
* Value. Feels rather lackluster considering you can get high quality protein much cheaper from other brands ounce for ounce.

All in all a good powder that has an odd consistency and blends foamier than I prefer. Personally, I'm going to stick with my usual protein but this might be the right one for you depending what you're looking for.

review_title: Clear-headed energy but the taste is meh.
review_text:
Mindright Good Mood Superfood Bar with Ashwagandha, Cordyceps, Ginseng, MCT, Mood & Stress Support, Pack of 12 - Variety Pack-

I’m very torn on this product. I love the results in terms of how they make me feel but they don’t taste great. They remind me of some protein bars, very chewy and somewhat chalky/bland tasting. The blueberry one I found to be the best tasting but others in my office preferred the peanut butter.

The effect that these have or at least had on me was similar to an energy drink but without the crash. I recognize some of the ingredients from those that I’ve seen in energy drinks. The energy I feel from these is very clear-headed and focused. I didn’t feel jittery or anxious which is how I feel if I drink an energy drink.

The price point is high but after trying them I feel like they are most comparable as I mentioned to energy products. When I view it more as a supplement I can wrap my head around the cost. I eat half of a bar and that’s where I find the most benefit. Any more than that makes me feel a little too alert. I also suggest trying a little and waiting before eating more if it’s the first-time consuming one. I had a coworker try one and he said he had trouble sleeping but did enjoy the effects while he was working.

In the office, these got mixed feedback. Most of us enjoyed the alertness we got from them but didn’t like the taste. There were a couple of coworkers that simply didn’t like them but for the most part, we all came to the same conclusion. These did go fast though. Overwhelmingly my coworkers and I felt the effects were worth it even if we didn’t enjoy the taste all that much.

I do recommend giving them a try because there were a couple that did like both the taste and the effects. Largely though we all landed on the same verdict, great as a supplement but not the best tasting. They aren’t terrible in taste but I wouldn’t go out of my way to eat one if it didn’t have the effects it does. I’ve come to enjoy the mid-day pep these provide. I would reorder them solely for that purpose. I think because it only takes half of a bar to produce those effects for me the price is worth it.

review_title: Interesting Idea, Not Sure About the Execution
review_text:
An all-in-one workout formula sounds amazing. Being able to take everything prior to the workout and hope that it works as it should is a dream that many of us probably have when it comes to our fitness.

This is interesting in many ways. First, you are getting just two servings. It includes a face cover, which is actually pretty neat. Otherwise, you cut open the package and pour it into the mixing glass to drink. It was a bit caked up in the packaging, but I was able to get most of the formula out and into the glass.

The taste wasn't terrible. I will say it is better than any BCAA/Post-Workout beverage as I didn't catch an aftertaste. However, the effect simply isn't there. I felt a slight energy kick for the first 10 minutes or so of my workout. I then just went back to how I feel when I drink water before, during, and after. There was nothing afterwards either.

Perhaps the idea of an all-in-one would require more to the formulation with a better delayed release? I don't know. Maybe it was more than that given that I didn't feel anything at all, nor did I recover as well as I do with a regular BCAA formula.

Nice face cover though, for sure. :)

review_text:
Highly recommended to try if you are experiencing knee pain. My moderate knee pain when standing from a sitting position has been gone for a year from a 1/2 scoop a week.

I'm late 40s, 6'3" and 225 lbs and I was experiencing moderate pain in my right knee when I stood up from a sitting position to the point I routinely used my arms to push myself up to help lessen the pain. I had been taking chondroitin and glucosamine and fish oil a few times a week for several years yet I still developed knee pain. For reference, my knees have been creaking when I walk up stairs with no pain since my mid 20s.

Almost a year ago I looked for a way to help with the knee pain and from internet searches I came across collagen. This product seems to be the best among the various types and sources of collagen so I thought I would give it a try and I'm glad I did. I started with a half scoop of the collagen. After three days I noticed I felt less knee pain when I stood up from a chair while pushing up with my arms. It took a few seconds for me to realize that I had taken the collagen a few days earlier and maybe that's the reason why I had less pain.

I waited a few more days to see if my knee pain would lessen and it did not, so after a week I took another 1/2 scoop. A few days later I noticed even less pain and figured I would keep at 1/2 scoop a week. By the third time taking collagen I was able to stand up from a sofa chair without using my arms and had no knee pain. The lack of pain surely was due to the collagen but my knees still creak when I go up stairs and stand up from a sitting position. I didn't want to push it by doing deep knee bends as if I had new knees but I do moderate exercises knee bending exercises and feel no immediate pain (only latent pain the next day or so if I overdo it).

Although the collagen has helped my knee pain when standing, it has not helped my knees in other ways such as pain from prolonged kneeling or squatting (prolonged being only a few minutes). The collagen did not help other minor joint pains (hip, elbow, shoulder) I get from exercise or being in certain sitting or sleeping positions for long periods. Because this worked so well for my knee pain I got a jar for my dad and he took 2-3 scoops most days for about a month but it did not help with his lower back pain. He is in his 70s and uses a walker and scooter due to lower disc and nerve problems.

The plain taste of this collagen is a horrible fishy flavor with water alone, but with coconut water it is fine. I'm glad the makers didn't flavor the collagen and left the flavoring to the customer.

review_text:
While this formula obviously has some good ingredients and a decent supply of many vitamins in it, it's what is not listed on the label that is bothering me. I am a Type II diabetic and already have to swallow a huge handful of pills everyday, so I was looking for a drinkable multivitamin to lessen to burden of digging through bottles of pills each day.

However, one thing that I did not immediately notice on the nutrient and ingredients label was the large number of calories and carbohydrates in each serving. It includes a whopping 48 calories per ounce, which includes 11 carbohydrates (and zero protein). I know from experience that the only way of packing that many calories and carbs into such a small serving is if something has LOTS of sugars in it. Yet if you look at the label it does not include the required disclosure of how many grams of sugars each serving includes.

When you look at the raw ingredient list you can see that it includes fruits, so there has to be sugars in the formula. It is mandatory by law that these amounts are listed on the label. However, it is not to be found anywhere. This is clearly something that the FDA should look into as failure to list these amounts is a danger to diabetics such as myself and others who are trying to avoid sugars and reduce their weight.

review_text:
I have to admit, this is probably the most robust and inclusive pre-workout powder I've ever tried...and I've tried many. It's got a lot of electrolytes and other things that are good for people to have in general, but especially for those on Keto (which I am on).

Interestingly, the physical size of the servings are the largest of any workout powder I've used. It looks like a protein powder scoop. It's not bad or good, it's just interesting. In my case, I shouldn't have filled my glass with so much water when I tried this.

Speaking of which, it doesn't dissolve as easily as other powders. I really had to mix it. The good news is, once I mixed it, it stayed mixed. Most of the other ones don't dissolve completely enough and there's a lot of residue at the bottom (unless you put them in a container you can shake or you use a blender, although either of those will probably help with this powder as well). Also, this powder is more finely ground than others. Again, not really bad or good, it just is.

The flavor is...well...pink lemonade. It tastes almost like the old crystal light mixes I had growing up. No medicine taste or after taste. That's good.

I think the biggest issue people will have is that this supplement is about 30 bucks (at the time of this writing) and you get 20 servings. That's a lot of money per serving. I know it's a robust supplement but come on. That's putting it into elite status. Just a thought.

Overall, I do like it and it does work. I also don't get a massive heart race from it. Good stuff.

This is such a bad take on Collagen powder. For anyone who actually enjoys taking this, sorry not sorry but I actually do not like this at all. It also has this really gross taste and smell that I want nothing to do with. Needless to say, the tub I purchased is probably in a dump somewhere, still full.
Since then I’ve moved to Wholesome Wellness and I have no regrets at all. In comparison to Ancient Nutrition, Wholesome Wellness is way better in terms of quality, taste, smell, and mixability. I can take their Collagen Powder with any drink I want, both hot and cold, because it dissolves in seconds. The best part about their collagen powder’s taste is that it doesn’t have one at all. The same goes for smell. So far it’s been working well for me and I do not regret moving to their brand at all. I encourage you all to do the same.

review_text:
I took a good 30 days before writing this review because, after all, I am hoping to tell you how well this performs. And, as you can imagine, that's very difficult to say. I will say that I've taken Creatine on and of for nearly 25 years now and, for me anyway, the hard part is the loading phase. Taking some amount multiple times a day until it is built up in your system before moving to the maintenance phase. I mean, really...I'd do great for 3 or 4 days then go out of town and...dang...forgot my creatine. Or I'd miss doses here and there and have to wonder if it had an impact or not. But this stuff...

I took it 3 times a week about 30 minutes before hitting the gym, but it didn't seem to kick in till the end of my workout. I started taking it just short of an hour before the gym and I could see the effects immediately. It definitely is easy to take - not that powder wasn't. Creatine doesn't taste like much so I would usually just through a tablespoon in my mouth and wash it down with water. For this "liquid" form I just took a swig straight from the bottle. But....is it REALLY a liquid? I suppose if you consider a mildly gritty creatine mixed with a goop the consistency of maple syrup a "liquid" then, yes...its a liquid. But seriously, it does pour easily enough and it's easy to swallow with or without a chaser. The flavor is fine, to - very much like a lemon drop.
I haven't done the math but I kind of doubt its as cheap as the powdered stuff, but then...you only need to take it on workout days - if that's what you're using it for. I am 51 and I take creatine not only as part of my strength training routine but also to help my muscles retain a bit of water. For that reason I MAY start taking the powdered version again now that this trial is over, but...maybe not. Its just SO DANG CONVENIENT

product_title: Muscle Feast Grass-Fed Whey Protein Isolate, All Natural Hormone Free Pasture Raised, Mocha, 5lb (94 Servings)
review_text:
I bought Muscle Feast Grass Fed Whey Protein Isolate because I was looking for grass fed isolate from cows not treated with hormones, and this fit the bill. There were a lot of positive reviews, but I did notice some newer reviews talked about a change to the formula that made it too sweet.

So here's my take, as a person who's used a lot of whey isolate products. The vanilla Muscle Feast protein powder mixes as well as any powder with relatively few ingredients, which is to say not quite as well as those with additional ingredients, but that's okay - I wanted less ingredients, more protein. The stevia taste is very strong and overwhelms with its sweet/bitter taste.

As a very regular stevia user, I know what I consider too much stevia, and this was definitely want over the line off too much. But here's what I did about it. For every 20 grams of powder, I add a slightly heaping teaspoon of unsweetened cocoa powder, which really takes the edge off. And sometimes a teaspoon of light sour cream, as well. And suddenly the protein drink is much more pleasant, even enjoyable. I tried a vanilla powder product, but I didn't like the end result as much. Still, if you have one you like, I'd say it's worth a shot.

I talked to a very courteous Muscle Feast rep about the overwhelming stevia taste, and that rep said that some people had complained that the powder wasn't sweet enough. They said that some users mix half unflavored powder and half vanilla, but that would also get rid of the vanilla taste, which (for me) works very well with the cocoa powder.

One other thing I wanted to point out is that Muscle Feast doesn't put certain information or icons on their powder to inform potential users. For example, if you look at the questions on the product page, you'll discover that the milk is sourced from Germany. You won't, however, find that into on the bottle. And while the find print of a longish paragraph on the bottle says this product is undenatured, it's not shown on the bottle in a way that stands out.

WIth my cocoa powder tweak, I'm happy with Muscle Feast Grass Fed Whey Protein Isolate, and I've ordered some unflavored to add to pancakes and breads. It's nice that there's a product for a reasonable price that hits all my wants for a protein powder. My previous favorite is about $50 for 2 pounds (Opportuniteas), and their chocolate has sugar (I'm diabetic, so staying away from sugar), so Muscle Feast's price for 2 pounds is definitely wallet-friendlier.

review_title: Best chocolate flavored protein powder ever!
review_text:
Being over 30, my wife and I are doing our best to win the “battle of the bulge” by eating healthfully. We really enjoy fruit smoothies and protein drinks, since these make it easier for us to get nutrition on the go. This protein powder makes that even more pleasant.

The ingredients are simple and all-natural: It’s got brown rice, quinoa and coconut proteins, cocoa powder, chocolate flavoring, acacia gum powder, monk fruit and vanilla flavoring. It’s vegan, organic and non-GMO. There’s no dairy, gluten, sugar or soy. Since there’s no pea protein in this powder, I don’t experience the gas I get from products containing that ingredient. I’m not phlegmy from dairy or experiencing other issues from products commonly present in other drink mixes.

I love the taste of this powder. When I stir it into ice-cold dairy-free almond milk or similar beverage, it blends well and tastes yummy. Adding frozen banana and nut butter in the blender makes a delicious “chunky monkey” smoothie.

This is really great in the protein ball recipe a friend gave me. You combine 3 scoops of Botanica Health Organic Vegan chocolate protein powder with 3 cups of rolled oats. Stir in 1 cup of almond butter and 1/4 cup of honey. Add up to 1/3 cup almond, oat or coconut milk, until the mixture is easy to shape into balls. You may want to roll the balls in more powder, so they don’t stick together. Store in a Ziploc bag or plastic container until you are ready for a quick, tasty snack.

It’s a bit pricy at almost $50 for the 29.6 oz. container I got. That’s $1.69 an ounce, or about $2.50 per serving. It’s cheaper than you’d pay for a health drink at a store, but a pretty big chunk of change to drop at one time.

review_text:
I was first introduced to this product at a Spartan race, where I happened to win an unlimited weekend supply for the race. Their team was great, and since then I've started listening to their podcast as well.

On to the actual product. I was pleasantly surprised when I tried out the product the day before the race, and so I decided to fill one of my hydration bladders with it for the race as well. I felt like I got a little boost without any weird jitters.

I ended up buying a tub of my own, and am currently using it as a pre-workout for 60-minutes resistance training sessions. Right now I am cutting, and usually lift early in the morning. This stuff gives me a nice even buddy of energy and send to last through the workout. I've tried a number of inexpensive pre-workout supplements and they either didn't work out made me feel weird.

A couple complaints. First, the tub was a nightmare to get open. The protective seal broke about 9 tubes when trying to open it. It was frustrating. Second, the website mentions suggested "scoops" for intensity. Mine did not come with a scoop. The nutrition label was also not add complete as I would expect. I didn't see a calorie count on it. Finally, it did not mix very easily. It took a lot of stirring, and I still had some red chunks in it.

Overall, I like the product and will continue to use it. Does it help with recovery and everything else the company claims? I really can't quantify that, but it definitely helps my workouts out. I will continue to use this.

However, as I lost my primary care doctor to the pandemic and there is yet another surge going on, swamping our local medical system right now, this is not the best time for a high-risk senior citizen to move around town trying to find a new doctor. So, for the moment, I've been looking for products that can alleviate the symptoms until I can find a doctor and get the underlying issue resolved.

This is the second product I've tried, the first being a peppermint oil caplet. The peppermint oil immediately slowed down the diarrhea and the explosiveness but did nothing for the sometimes-intense gassiness. It also left my stomach in a lot of roiling upset. This Healthy Gut powder also slowed down the diarrhea but also eased down the gassiness and felt much gentler on my stomach, quieting down the gut turmoil. So, of the two products, this was very much the more effective, all-around treatment. The only reason I did not give it five stars is the price. If one continued to need this product on an ongoing basis, that could quickly add up to quite a bit of money.

There are several caveats I need to include here. The first is that this powder, like the peppermint oil, helped with the symptoms but hasn't dealt with the underlying issue. The second is that human beings are not one size fits all. Different people may react to the same product in different ways. So your mileage may indeed vary. Finally, the powdered drink can be a bit intense. The first time I tried it, the drink itself left me feeling bloated for a while. After several days of drinking it, sometimes it goes down easy for me. Other times, that bloated feeling comes back, making it harder to drink. The relief it provides is worth it though, so I do drink the suggested amount before each meal. Good luck. If you try this gut powder, I hope it helps you.

review_title: Enjoy In A Smoothie But Don’t Know If Healthy Given Extra Iron & No Info Re Heavy Metals (3.5 Stars)
review_text:
I’m on a weight loss program and have an allowance for some added protein and a few servings of fruit every day. I’ve been making smoothies with Amazing Grass Organic Plant Protein Blend (Vanilla) and organic frozen berries and bananas. I like the taste and texture best if I add yogurt and/or nonfat milk as a base, but I’m mostly using water or a mix of water and a little yogurt to keep calories down.

I have no issue getting enough protein as I can always eat egg whites, tofu, lean meat, etc. But I feel satisfied drinking a smoothie with this powder as the protein tides me over, and I like that I’m getting in my fruit, some hydration and hopefully some nutrients from the added fruit and vegetable blend. This is also easy for me to digest. I enjoy this protein powder enough to use it daily, but I won’t for the two reasons noted in my last paragraph.

I do find this has a strong stevia aftertaste. I don’t mind it, but those adverse to that stevia taste may not like this powder (though they might be able to add a lot of stuff to hide the taste). Also, the powder is a little gritty even blended. That doesn’t bother me, especially since my smoothies also have texture from berry seeds. I find the grit less noticeable when blended with milk and yogurt instead of water.

I do dislike two things. First, this has added iron. That’s great if you need it, but unnecessary iron can have negative health consequences (especially for kids) and it’s been confirmed by blood test that I don’t need it. Second, Amazing Grass won’t disclose the amount of heavy metals in the powder. That concerns me as studies have found levels I’m not comfortable with in popular plant-based protein powders. I enjoy this powder, but I don’t even know if it’s healthy and will use it in moderation only. 3.5 stars.

product_title: MusFit Clearly Superior Clear Whey Protein Isolate 20g Pineapple, 30 Servings
review_text:
Useful may be an usual description to use for a food product, but certainly not unwarranted.

A while back I discovered 'clear' protein mixes to make a nice, tasty (-ish) beverage to supplement protein in my diet (this utility being the reason for the term 'useful'). I really dislike protein shakes (no matter what I mix with, or the type of protein or presentation (whey, soy, isolate, flavored, unflavored, casein, etc.), they leave me feeling slightly nauseous - I wouldn't be surprised if it's psychosomatic though.)), but I like the idea of shakes. That is to say, drink some protein without having to prep a protein-high meal, though of course I do eat those as well.

For a while I was using Isopure Infusions but had a couple issues; if you missed mixing some of the powder it would turn into this plasticy, caulk-like putty stuck to the inner lid and/or drink spout. Then there's the cost; the Isopure is in line with most protein products, so I wasn't too concerned when buying it, but I do search for cheaper product occasionally (which is how I found MusFit). The flavor is okay but not great - I tended to add in some pre-workout or Propel drink mix to improve the flavor before/after a workout as appropriate.

Then I found MusFit and decided to try it out. At the time of me writing this, the MusFit is $13 cheaper than the Isopure. This adds up for me as I tend to go through 1.5 to 2 jugs a month.

The flavor for me is much better (I've only tried the pineapple flavor so far). I like this product straight, though it does mix nicely with my pre-workout. I'll grab a premixed drink out of the fridge first thing in the morning and it is delicious as a first beverage.

I also find the MusFit blends better for me (I use/d Blender Bottles for both products - shaking for 2 to 3 minutes) as I haven't discovered any lumpy surprises.

As to the effectiveness? Well, that's hard to speak to as I use different dietary supplements to hit my numbers. I have been buying this particular product for almost 10 yrs now. Of all of the proteins I have tried, this is the one my body tolerates the best. It also has a complete amino acid makeup which is noted on the package. I will not buy a protein powder that does not list its amino acid breakdown on it because 9 times out of 10 those powders offer little nutritional value and alot of sugar.

I have sjrogrens and other autoimmune issues. Remarkably the soy in this does not cause a flare, but I do not have a high soy allergy. As for taste and mixing, this is the type of shake you can make with just water and it will be perfect. it blends well yet is heavy enough that when you open it you dont end up with a counter full of powder. Remember this is made with Rice, Pea, and Soy for protein. Protip: Add a packet of orange Emergen-c to it and it makes a lower calorie version of an Orange Julius that wont give you diabetes.

Mixes well with milks, juices, sparkling water, and plain water
Has high nutritional value - Amino Acid breakdown is on the label
Vegetarian Protein: Rice, Pea, Soy
Decent sugar: Balanced sugar, but if you want lower carb, the Spiru-tein Gold line is better.

Cons:
None. Though word to the wise, this product has spirulina in it which means, once mixed, must not be left out sit in room temperature or heat. If it spoils, you can kiss whatever container it was in goodbye (unless it is made of glass). Speaking from the experience of the occasional shake bottle left in car during the summer over a weekend. review_title: easy to eat on the go, hint of pineapple, lightly sweet
review_text:
Healthy snack bars can be hit or miss. This is a hit, for me (yay!). I tend to keep a few snack bars on me as I don't have a chance to take a mid day meal. The snack bars are simply easy to grab and my choice often depends on how easy they are to eat if I can't eat it all at once, and if I will need to pick the food out from my teeth or not.

These bars are soft and chewy. It is easy to break off pieces and eat on the run. I can take a bite here and there, or pull off a piece as I want it.

The bar doesn't get stuck all up in my teeth like some harder, stickier textured bars do. I might bite a piece of quinoa or crisp rice later, but I don't have a coating glomed onto my teeth.

Bland enough to not want to gobble up the box, but tasty enough to be a pleasant eating experience. Really works for times when I just need something, and I can't have it be complicated or messy to eat.

I like the texture of the compressed oats, quinoa, crispy rice.. as well as the hint of pineapple. I love pineapple and would love a more pronounced pineapple flavor (or maybe dried bits of it, mmm)--but this is well balanced. A little sweet, has a good mouth feel (soft, chewy, and any bit of crunch is from the crisp bits).

Reminds me of something I would make at home, without having to make it :)

Ingredients:
Oats, Crispy Rice, Glucose, *Quinoa, *Panela, *Andean Lupin, Coconut.

Organic Panela =unrefined whole cane sugar

Organic Andean Lupin= nutritionally dense legume. Closely related to peanuts and soy bean

I had gastric bypass almost 5 years ago and I am always looking for ways to help supplement my protein intake. I saw this powder and decided to give the chocolate a try.

Pros: I love the individual packets. I love the nutritional value since I am supposed to stay low carb and low sugar.

I threw in a pack with some water and shook it as directed. It blended well, there were not any clumps (Which you tend to get if the liquid is too warm, keep it below 140 degrees F people).

My first sip was a bit meh. Second sip was actually pretty decent. It does taste a bit too sugary for me, but that could just be how my tastes have changed since my surgery.

The powder was packed well, it was in a vacuumed sealed bag, which I suspect was done to fix some of the other issues I was reading about for example the packets sticking together, etc.

All in all it is a pretty decent protein powder. I did not feel sick drinking it, which tends to happen with me and powders. It was a decent chocolate flavor, and I think the next time I drink this I will try using milk of some sort to see if that cuts down on the sugary taste for me.

review_title: A Tasty Improvement on a Great Product
review_text:
I have been using Clif Bars since about the time the company was founded. They have always been the best tasting bar in this category. These bars are no exception. In fact, I like them better than the originals.

Each of these flavors is based on a classic Cliff Bar. However, I like that they are just a bit less sweet. It's a nice balance. I have found that they sweet part is an extra drizzle of frosting like material on the bar. I was worried that this was going to melt and be a mess. However, after 4 or 5 late summer mountain bike rides with these in my pack I am happy to report that they are no messier than the old bars. I also like the addition of almonds or peanuts in most of these. It gives a nice texture.

Overall I really think Clif did a good job of making an already good product better. If you like the original bars you will probably really like these.

review_text:
I’ve been buying protein bars for years now since I lift several days a week and these ones are by far my favorite out of anything else ive ever tried

I also love that they’re low in carbs and added sugar

I’d say there’s just a few downsides but they might not be a negative depending on who you are
1 they can be a little drying for your mouth
2 I dislike that they have palm oil, I feel like these would taste the same with a different ingredient that doesn’t cause massive destruction of the rainforests
3 the protein content isn’t that high especially compared to the amount of fat in each bar (and compared to other protein bars), but they did recently change the recipe to go from 10g to 13/14g so that’s nice

Still overall really delicious and a good protein snack option

review_title: Delicious addition to any beverage to fill you up and get you going!
review_text:
The members of our household have been trying to lose weight. We need foods that are high in protein and low in carbs to facilitate that process. I am not a fan of either the Keto Diet or its predecessor, the Atkins Diet, because forcing your body into a constant state of ketosis can be very dangerous. One member of my family was actually hospitalized with ketosis several years ago. However, foods that are high in plant and animal proteins and healthy oils help your body build muscle and burn fat.

The ingredients in this powder are great. It contains MCT oil powder (made from coconut oil and acacia gum), fava protein, pea protein, vanilla, prebiotic fiber, brown rice peptide, coconut flavor, sea salt, marine algae, and stevia to sweeten it. It's soy free, dairy free, gluten free, vegan and mostly organic.

This powder blends really well with just about any cold beverage, and it tastes amazing in fruit smoothies. Unlike other products containing pea protein, this did not give me gas, but it did give my spouse some digestive discomfort. I really liked how it curbed my hunger and lasted all morning when I had it for breakfast. Unlike whey protein, this product has a good dose of fiber, so I didn't get constipated.

At almost $45 for a one-and-a-half pound container, I feel like this product is way overpriced. You get 15 servings for that amount, paying about $3 for a 3 ounce scoop of powder in 10 ounces of liquid for each serving. If you want something healthy and tasty, but don't mind the high price tag, then enjoy!

My husband has been working out and lifting weights since he was a Freshman in high school and on the wrestling team. As an adult, he has worked hard to become a strong and consistent body builder, weight lifter, and trainer and has done well and succeeded. He has tried so many different supplements to help him along his journey, and this was definitely at the bottom of his list of likes.

He has a list of requirements when taking supplements, and this supplement only met one of them.
First off I will start with what led me to choosing this for him as an option to try out while he is getting his gains on.
1) The packaging is really nice, and I like the details of the picture and the design of the label. To be honest, the design and the clear label is probably one of my favorites of the ones that he has tried in the past.
2) The amount of servings for the price. I am so used to spending $50 on a 30 serving pre-workout, so having this price being slightly lower and including an extra 10 servings I jumped all over it.
3) He liked the ingredients for he most part.

Now onto his list of what he requires when he is taking pre-workout.
1) Cost - This is right around what we normally pay so he didn't hate this until he realized that he did not like the flavor. And with the servings being 10 more than what he is used too, he was excited for that.
2) Mix ability, it has to mix well. He said that this just did not mix as well as some of the others he has used.
3) Smell, he said right away that it smelled like stale coffee and he was not impressed to take it further and taste it.
4) Taste, he said it was disgusting and he would not recommend this at all. He said he could taste the coffee flavor, but it tasted "old and dusty". He was not impressed at all.

So this was not something that he would consider recommending to anyone, and he will recommend and share his supplements with guys that he works out with at the gym. He gave it a zero stars, I added one for the reasons I mentioned first.

review_title: Glad I tried it, but...edited after two tries
review_text:
First Review with Banana Cinnamon, Original :Because there literally is so little fill value in this product, I would highly suggest adding in Hemp Hearts or Flaxseed Meal, or Chia seeds; something, anything to feel full. I don't know when people say that it was "thick", they must be adding in other products. The shake itself is THIN. I probably will be getting more because the flavor, taste, etc is GOOD (it is overly sweet for many, this I would agree), and really fantastic, having had Pea protein prior (grittiness problems). Yet as a meal replacement it really needs more 'bulk', otherwise, it's a good protein supplement, ( just don't expect to feel full). Later, I was completely surprised that while it was sweet, once the sweet tasted wore off, the hunger feeling faded. Interesting! The satiety lasted upwards to 5 hours. This is not the norm for me with anything sweet.

The second shake I added a frozen banana to it and a tablespoon of flaxseeds. The chocolate flavor agreed is kind of thin, don't think "Carnation Instant Breakfast" here. If you want it "more chocolate" I think i would add some chocolate powder. The frozen banana thickened it up well and the Flaxseeds help with not only extra fiber, but keeping the sugar taste down. Most might not add in Banana, but I needed the vitamins. Okay, this was excellent in flavor and again, this lasted a heck of a long time by comparison of straight Pea Protein, and certainly tastes a heck of a lot better.

Yet:
Originally gave it 4 stars, staying there, just because the overall cost of this product is Just mostly prohibitive. Not everyone has $40 for 15 servings. I somehow wonder, what in half a jar does this solve? Yes, it is tasty, but it doesn't have potassium, so if you need a true electrolyte balance, this won't help. It isn't exactly brimming with other vitamins as well. To get that you'll need to add in additional food source to make it a true meal replacement. Marketing is going to have to work with this one a bit in my honest opinion for this product to be called a meal replacement. A protein enhancement? Yes. And if this is your goal, this one tastes good, but again, for 1 drink per day it's going to be expensive.

review_title: Good flavor and definitely creamy; Funny packaging
review_text:
The flavor is good. Not my favorite but I do like it. However, there are some things worth noting. I'll give the good and bad.

PROS
- Good flavor: I like the vanilla flavor. I wasn't sure what creamy meant as a flavor but that's actually a good description. Creamy vanilla.
- High protein
- Keto Friendly: Nice if you care about the carbs.
- Mixes well

CONS
- Scoop size: This was annoying at first. Look at the pictures. I have a few blender bottles. One has a 3.5 inch mouth and the other has a 2 in. mouth. The size of the scoop was too big for my 2 in. bottle. It was difficult to use quickly. In the picture, you can see the scoop with the 3.5 in. blender bottle. Imagine that with a 2 in. mouth.
- Can too short: At first, I had to dig for the scoop. That's fine. Really not a problem. However, after the first use I had dig in circles to get the scoop back in the can. Obviously this problem goes away after a few uses but it was annoying. Just keep the scoop outside the can.

I still give it four stars. Some might not like the creamy flavor but that's a preference thing. The scoop thing isn't a big deal but with the cons together I docked a single star. It's just an inconvenience. Use a smaller scoop and say a serving is two scoops. Still, I'll use it to the bottom of the can.

review_title: The highest amount of protein per dollar
review_text:
I've tried a lot of different protein powders over the years. I go through a lot of it and for a while I was buying Muscle Milk, which was inexpensive when bought in a 5 lb. bag. The taste was OK, but I began to take a serious look at how much of the powder was actually protein (here's a hint-- not as much as I thought).

Because I'm a bit obsessive about these things, I made a spreadsheet to compare several different brands. I looked at grams of protein per serving, number of servings per container, and cost. This allowed me to calculate how many grams of protein I was actually getting per container (not just how much powder).

Gold Standard came out on top. Though the price is higher than some other powders, I can get more grams of protein per dollar spent than with any of the other commonly-available brands that I looked at. There may be a better value out there, but I limited my search to stuff I could buy from Amazon.

The taste is... OK. I've tried a couple of different ones so far. Double rich chocolate tastes no better or worse than most of the other chocolate protein powders I've tried. It's a bit less sweet, and I suspect that there are fewer grams of sweetener in this powder than some of the others, but I haven't cared to look.

I tried one of the strawberry flavors and the taste was very diluted, even though I mix it with only a small amount of water. Neither one tasted bad, but there's no doubt you're drinking them for nutrition rather than enjoyment.

I believe the best tasting protein powder I ever tried was Syntha 6 chocolate cake batter. It's been a while but I remember it having a very rich chocolate flavor. It doesn't provide as much protein per dollar (at least at the time of my analysis), but I may try it again out of curiosity.

Optimum generally has a pretty good reputation for protein powder, and I've been happy enough with it that I'm on my 6th or 7th tub from them. The flavor is OK but not great when mixed with water (I haven't tried it with milk), it mixes easily, and it has a high protein-per-dollar ratio. I don't think you can go wrong here.

review_title: Whey Different Than Milk Based Protein Powders
review_text:
My first experience trying this was alarming. The least of which was I had to really dig down deep to find the scoop and got product all over my hand (and eventually shirt). So for those that say there is no scoop, try REALLY digging around!

I used the same amount of oat milk I use with the Whey Protein Powder and ended up with thick sludge stuck like denser than peanut butter. Yikes! So I added more liquid and it was fine but you end up having to drink more overall liquid for the same amount of protein as Whey.

Then I forgot I bought unflavored. I almost threw up. It was like drinking cardboard blended with tofu. Definitely will need some flavoring liquid/powder or a half cup at least of berries to blend with this stuff, or get vanillar flavored oat milk, or SOMETHING. Definitely will try a flavored version next time. You'd be nuts to drink this stuff straight. Gross.

A little background on why I bought this product:

I've been using Milk Protein Powders occasionally (just in the 24 hours after resistance/weight training) to make sure I had adequate protein intake. I preferred the Phase 8 brand as it was slow release, their flavors were delicious, and the powder blended very easily even with a small amount of water or oat milk.

Recently being diagnosed with Prostate Cancer, I discovered in my research that studies show Caseinate (a product in Milk Protein Powders) can be pro cancer, but go figure, other studies show Whey Protein can be protective. Unfortunately the Phase 8 brand has more Caseinate than other Whey Protein brands as they add it specifically as an additional ingredient. Furthermore, studies have shown Soy Isoflavones can be protective against cancer.

So I decided to switch to Soy even though Whey has been shown to promote muscle growth a bit better. (Best is to eat clean, low-fat protein sources -- but for post-workout that's a lot of food so a protein powder helps you get there without having to pig out on chicken.

I still crave carbs, but that is just something you have to decide to avoid, even though you are going to think about it. Maybe a lot. The vanilla tastes great, and will be a permanent addition for my breakfast every day. It's less expensive to buy it on Amazon with Prime than it is to go to your local grocer, unless there is a super sale buy/coupons, and then it goes back to a higher retail price. review_title: taste like chocolate chip cookie dough!
review_text:
I like any of the Orgain protein bars of this style. Has a good texture, and is not too sweet. This one definitely reminds me of cookie dough, so they did a good job with it. The initial bite has that protein taste though. Seems to simmer down with more bites. Something unique about these bars that I like.

Mixed reviews, but I decided to give them a try anyway because I like Orgain products, AND it was on sale, bringing it closer to $1 per bar. I bought the S'mores, and I find them incredible. Then I bought this Chocolate Chip Cookie dough, and it tastes like cookie dough, and the texture too. Like the cookie dough you can get in rolls in the refridgerated sections. But slightly more firm for handling. Very interesting.

As with the Smores option, here too I expected a strong protein taste, and at first I did taste a little of that. But I think the initial opening of the packet released some off gassing, and so my first bite seemed to taste protein-y. However, the rest of it was divine. I didnt gobble it all down at once. Remainder of my review is the same as my review for the smores option, so I will just copy it over here.

I tend to chomp on these through my work day, so I take a bite then set aside for awhile, then return to it as needed. I work a physical job and so it isn't easy to just eat a meal. I also need something that can stick to my ribs. I was really pleasantly surprised that I could eat just this and get through my day. I think I had an apple (cut up for same ease of munching) along side it. It wasn't a fluke, because i did it again the next work day, and had same results. So the protein used is a long burner. Coffee, orgain bar, sliced up apple. All good. All day.

Taste? good. Not too sweet
Texture? awesome. Has a good chew. If warm (like sitting in car) it gets a little goey, but it stays solid- no mess. I like the bits of chocolate. Adds good mouth feel.

I'm a big fan of loading up my purse with snack bars-- again, I work a physical job with no real breaks. I like knowing I have something to nibble on as need be. I would also grab for this when I want something candy bar like, and not worry about taking the sugar hit. I just find it all around pleasant, and will likely buy it again (though preferably on sale), and likely try other flavors.

review_title: Two (2) Scoops Please; But What Formula Today?
review_text:
Mild, unique chocolate aroma
Mild chocolate flavor
No clumping
Made in USA
Soft powder
GMP

Considerations
Different from listing’s picture
Has artificially made ingredients – sucralose most concerning

The bag
The powder arrived in a 9” inch tall, 5½” wide and near 2 ½” deep sealed plastic like food type bag that the top can be torn off and then allowed to reseal, with no issue.

Aroma & Taste
There is no accounting for smell or taste, however, chocolate is universal, and this has a mild, delicate aroma and taste of a chocolate (water based) shake.

The Great Debate
The science is kind of thin surrounding the benefits of these kinds of supplements, however, it’s universally known that cultures with heavily biased protein-based diets may grow taller. Now whether there are health benefits using this product will not be outlined or debated here, as the reader can make that conclusion independently. Notwithstanding, this writer wanted to take advantage of those benefits we understand are associated with taking this supplement which is marketed toward growth in height for children.

Value
This offers pricing that is competitive with other supplements that have some, but not all the same ingredients. These powders never seem to be inexpensive. There is a price to pay for results, I guess. I have never seen such vitamins and minerals targeted so specifically for children and their growth, so this is where the value seems to come into play. I am happy to have selected this to at least try, the results are still pending, as any results are measured in months, not days.

The Brand
I never heard of the TrueHeight brand before selecting this.

GMP
This was reported to have been made using GMP (good manufacturing practices).

Allergy Warnings
This was manufactured in a facility that processes milk, eggs, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, soy and wheat, and that those ingredients may be in this powder.

The powder
The powder is very soft. The texture is smooth. The powder, with enough mixing, for the most part, dissolved in water in a fairly short time. The powder did not clump, like a rock, in the bag or in the liquid.

Ingredients
The powder is made in the USA, from globally sourced ingredients. We would suggest reading the label on the bag in the listing, however, that listing’s picture is different from what we received. I’m not happy about that. Either have the formula down pat or not, but I do not like to be part of any experiment in formulation, and for that reason, a star is taken away.

Artificial sweetener
Has artificially made ingredients – sucralose most concerning. I will leave that to the reader to decide whether they want something that science had to create to make.

Best of both worlds
These have the best of both worlds, vitamins and minerals and a formula for growth. So, we can say goodbye to chewing or swallowing a hard pill that’s even close to these ingredients. I think this should be beneficial, only time will tell, and in this instance, I was given a bag with (15) servings, which is not going to last the many months needed to see results.

Digestion
No complaints if taken during or just after a meal.

Fresh product received
The date of manufacture was labeled. October 05, 2022, I received these at the start of December 2022. Expiration was labeled as being September 2024.

Always consult a healthcare professional prior to anyone taking a supplement.

I hope my thoughts were informative.

review_title: Caffeine the way I like it
review_text:
I have a shake every morning for breakfast, and since I don't drink coffee, I'm always looking for a means of perking me up without giving me the jitters. I'm what you would call "sensitive to caffeine" and I don't have the luxury of just guzzling huge amounts of it without having to get kids fed, dressed, and out the door before I workout. In short, I need a boost, but not TOO much of a boost.

So to that end I'm always on the lookout for powder I can mix with my shake that I can measure. And by that I mean the producer being honest about the amount of caffeine in the powder. If you ignore the hype (Jacked Factory? Okay), the company does a great job of clearly explaining how much caffeine you're dosing with. That's 180 mg, if you're wondering. So you know what you're getting, in addition to plenty of other supplements that are supposed to increase your workout performance. But really, I've learned it's the caffeine you feel the most.

To that end, although the container comes with 10 packages, I wouldn't dream of using one package alone. I divided it out into much smaller doses, which works fine for me. Even better, there's no artificial flavoring or coloring--it's cherry-flavored, but because I'm not a 12-year-old I don't need my powder to actually look red. Beet root powder does the trick.

Add this all up, and if you're looking for a measurable means of dosing caffeine in the morning, this will do nicely.

The Great Debate
The science always seems to be in question surrounding the benefits of supplements. Now whether there are health benefits using this product will not be outlined or debated here, as the reader can make that conclusion independently. Notwithstanding, this writer wanted to take advantage of those benefits we understand are associated with taking this supplement which is marketed toward heart health.

The bottle
The bottle of gummies arrived with a shrink-wrapped lid. The plastic bottle being (4.375”) inch tall and 3” in diameter (we’ve seen glass bottles in other supplements). The bottle did not have a “child-proof” lid (we prefer childproof, for safety’s sake). The bottle was sealed under the lid.

Aroma & Taste
These beet support gummies are noticeably firm. Now there is no accounting for taste, but the taste, was like pomegranate. The gummies have a stiff but smooth.

Value
This offers pricing that is competitive. I am happy to have selected this to try.

The Brand
I never heard of Kwala; they may have used a [contract] manufacturer of supplements. I suspect this since this is “manufactured for” them.

The gummies
These gummies are slightly stiff and/or firm but have some softness. The texture is smooth as I consumed (chewed) and the gummies “did not” stick to my teeth (which I prefer). These are not sugar free, which would have been nice, rather are like others. These have a dome shaped appearance and are about the size of a dime and several nickels stacked high thick.

Warning.
Do “not” eat more than the recommend amount, which is two (2) gummies per day, so says the label, that’s how potent these are.

Ingredients
These are made in the USA, which is noted on the bottle. Beet Root Powder, Grapeseed Extract, L-Arginine, L-Citrulline, Vitamin C & B12.

Best of both worlds
These have the best of both worlds, beet support in a gummy, so, I can say goodbye to swallowing a hard pill that’s even close to these ingredients. I think these beneficial to my health, only time will tell, and in this instance, I received a single bottle of (60) gummies.

Digestion
I felt no negative tummy consequences after taking.

Fresh product?
The date of manufacture was not labeled, but I could read the expiration, 06/2024. I received these during November 2022. The gummies were partially clumped together.

Always consult a healthcare professional prior to anyone taking a supplement.

I hope my thoughts were informative.

review_title: Tastes terrible, protein makeup is almost entirely pea protein
review_text:
I cannot stand the flavor of this, it does not taste like chocolate and it leaves an absolutely awful aftertaste with an paste-like after-texture (which was surprising because it seemed to mix into water relatively well).

Regardless of the flavor, I was also not impressed with the protein makeup. The packaging advertises that the 30g of protein comes from a combination of pea, alfalfa, pumpkin seed, and sunflower seed. That sounds good however the problem is that when you look at the ingredients list, the first three things listed are (in order) pea protein, cocoa powder, and natural flavors. Since ingredients are listed in the order of most-to-least prevalent, that means that there is more cocoa powder and "natural flavors" in this protein powder than pumpkin seed, alfalfa, and sunflower seed proteins. That's super shady marketing in my book because it means that the protein is basically entirely pea protein and the other three protein sources are only present in trace amount so that it appears to be a mix of protein sources.

There are some positives here, I'm impressed that 3g of fat and 4g of net carbs to each 30g of protein, that's better than a lot of vegan protein powders than I've seen.

It's sea moss in a gel? Well it was strange but I got it anyway.

As soon as I opened the jar I could smell the "ocean". As a kid, I grew up where there was a lot of iodine in the water and we smelled like it going home and called it the "ocean smell" That's what this product smells like, the ocean.

The range of recommended dosage of sea moss per day is very wide, as little as 1,200 mg and as much as 15,000. This product is pretty dense in nutrients based on the label and packs 10,000mg per serving so it's in the range on the high side as well as tons of other minerals.

The flavor is pretty strong but it doesn't bother me. I mix it with my pineapple/orange collagen drink and it tones it down a bit.

As with all the supplements that are all the rage these days, sea moss doesn't come cheap and if it's sustainably and fairly sourced then expect to pay more in general, if the product is processed and packaged into an easy to use form, then prices become premium.

I love to try new supplements and hope this works but most natural things take months to work and show results. I think sea moss might be one of those that are worth sticking with and I will update this review when I have more to contribute.

review_text:
I add collagen to my coffee. This product does not work well for that use case. It adds a noticeable and unpleasant taste to the coffee and it does not dissolve as well. It ruins the coffee. At the bottom of the cup there was undissolved collagen grit. I compared this directly to Vital Proteins Collagen Peptides. The Vital Proteins brand dissolved completely and had no impact on the coffee taste. The Vital Proteins brand advertises a neutral flavor, Ancient Nutrition does not.

The Ancient Nutrition brand adds vitamin C and probiotics, which other brands lack. Probiotics would be killed in hot coffee, which is another reason this product does not work for coffee or other very hot liquids. Some Vital Proteins varieties have vitamin C, but my Costco variety does not.

The Ancient Nutrition collagen is made from cow, eggshells, chicken bones, Haddock, Cod, and Pollock. Vital Proteins collagen comes only from cow.

As a collagen supplement for people who do not add it to coffee, the Ancient Nutrition brand is fine. I would consume this directly with water, like other powdered supplements. I would describe the taste as unpleasant. Other reviewers do not notice the taste, which is strange because it is very noticeable to me and the company makes no claims of having a neutral taste. I have had most of the popular brands of collagen over the years and there is a definite difference between the brands. The advertising says that you can add it to coffee, so I am lowering the rating to two stars, since it does not work for that. If they did not make that advertising claim then I would rate this three or four stars as a powdered supplement, versus a coffee additive.

review_text:
[[VIDEOID:ae1b8b3fbb7b1c4922f2d62d370ff9c2]] I have trusted JYM Products for quite some time, so when I recently discovered that they offer branched- chain amino acids (BCAAs), I was excited to check out their formula. Based on the research I've done (online and in person with trainers and athletes), the 2:1:1 ratio is the best for optimal results. (I've seen some companies increase leucine in their products, but a 5 or 6 ratio--rather than a 2--actually impedes the effectiveness of this trio of amino acids that includes leucine, isoleucine, and valine.)

This tub of 2:1:1 BCAAs has about 40 servings (at 10+ ounces each), so even though the tub isn't near full, which leaves plenty of room to scoop without spilling, there's well over a 30-day supply here.

It's recommended that a scoop be added to 10 ounces of water, but I feel like the grape candy flavor is really sweet and I like it better with around 13 ounces of water (and then I add ice) to tone it down. The directions say it can be used as a dietary supplement during a workout OR throughout the day when not training. People might take this supplement for a variety of reasons, but I take BCAAs to reduce muscle soreness and fatigue, as well as to help prevent muscle loss as I age. So far, this formula has helped me feel better post-workout AND I feel like I have more energy throughout the day on days when I do exercise and even on the days I don't train.

I have a difficult time getting the powder to mix well in water without the use of an electric whisk; even then, there is some minor grit as I drink it, and residue remains on the inside of my glass when I finish. I rinse the glass right away and swirl the water to get what's left and I drink it down so I don't waste any!

Each 9g serving (a single scoop) has 30 calories, 1g carbs, and 1 g total sugars. The branched-chain amino acids are L-Leucine (3g), L-Isoleucine (1.5g), and L-Valine (1.5g). Other ingredients include citric acid, dextrose, natural flavor, sucralose, calcium silicate, silicon dioxide, acesulfame potassium, and sunflower lecithin.

Allergen Note: This is produced with equipment that also manufactures products that may contain EGG, MILK, SOY, and TREE NUT ingredients.

review_text:
I used this powder for 2 months, and had no issues with the taste like some! My 1 star is because, as I got more interested in mushrooms, started learning and understanding the difference between mycelium and fruiting body.

Fruiting bodies have a MUCH higher amount of beneficial compounds when compared to mycelium. Mycelium tends to be grown on top of a substrate that's difficult to separate from the plant. That can be rice or grain and even wood (likely oat due to the "other ingredients" listed - certainly hope oat isn't a filler)

Further, why are we supplementing the powder with ginkgo (known to support brain function) and other herbs like holy basil and astragalus? Great herbs but not necessary if taking a pure mushroom powder.

Om (and many other sources) stand behind adding mycelium due to some of the benefits. I prefer fruiting body. I recommend you do your research and choose a powder that is in line w what you're looking for.

review_text:
I like the fact that this protein powder is made from just a very few, clean ingredients. The fact that it is vegan doesn’t matter much to me, but likely will to many people.
A couple of things to note:
A serving size is 1/2 cup. That’s a lot compared to most protein powders, and it means there are only 12 servings in a the bag.
210 calories per serving is quite high, almost twice as much as some other protein powders.
Fat content: 9 grams total fat, 7.5 grams saturated fat. Again, quite a bit higher than many other protein powders.
Now, other protein powders often rely on whey for their protein meaning the fat and calories will be lower. If you’re looking for a vegan product, in this case drawing the protein from chickpeas, the trade-off is higher fat and calories.
The vanilla flavor is good, has some sweetness thanks to the monk fruit. On its own, there’s a little aftertaste which I didn’t care for, but I mix my protein in a smoothie with other ingredients which negates the aftertaste.
I appreciate this being packaged in a bag rather than yet another huge plastic container, and I also like that there is no scoop included. Honestly, I have enough scoops to last me and everyone I know for the rest of our lives, so I’m fine being left to my own devices as far as measuring!

A good choice for protein powder, especially if you’re looking for a vegan option.
Made in the USA.

review_title: Used to be great, than they changed the formula
review_text:
This stuff used to be my go-to. I was happy to find a non-dairy based protein shake and drank it for multiple years. Than, about 6-12 months the formula changes and it just wasn't good anymore. I wrote the company and received the following:

"Thank you for taking the time to contact us regarding the problem you experienced with our EVOLVE Ideal Vanilla Protein Shake products. We share your concern and sincerely regret any inconvenience and concern this caused.

I want to assure you that the formula has not changed. Please know that I've shared the information you provided with the appropriate bottling facility for their review. I've also mailed out replacement coupons, which you should receive in about 10 days."

As a consumer, I can appreciate the company trying to make it right. Whether ill-informed or just downright deceitful, the formula 100% has changed. All these reviewers that wonder how anyone could rate this 5 star I am guessing didn't have these before the formula switch. There are other reviewers that have pointed out the same thing I have noticed, a definitive change in the taste, but not just that, also the consistency. The best way I can describe this is the way powder protein drinks taste when you make them at home. You know, that slightly chalky water-downed taste - that's what these taste like now where before they were extremely rich flavored. Considered these are fairly pricey, this is a big hit and I have stopped drinking them all together. I am still looking for a suitable replacement. Why mess up a good thing? Probably to save Pepsi some money since they acquired the makers of Evolve, CytoSport, back in early 2019. Hopefully it hurts enough to switch back, but my guess is the brand just dies off instead, at least their prepackaged product. It's an age old story.

review_title: Clear whey is a game changer for people who are sick of milkshake tasting protein powders
review_text:
Clear whey is a genius idea. Surprisingly, there are not too many products on the market. Looking at the ingredients, this is one of only about 2 or 3 clear whey brands I would use. This brand uses isolate (as opposed to concentrate) which is higher in protein. It has no sugar and no artificial sweeteners (a lot of other beans use sucralose or something similar). This brand, unlike the others, also doesn’t have anti-foaming agents. Yes, this foams a little, but the foam settles after 1 min. It also mixes quite easily and doesn’t leave large clumps. Bonus points for being made in the USA.

A+ for simple ingredients. Would love to see it made with grass fed whey though. It does leave a slight aftertaste in my mouth. Nothing awful, but my mouth feels slightly drier. Also, you could definitely dilute this down if you just want flavored water. 1 scoop in 32 oz would still be reasonable and still taste fine. Out of the two flavors I tried, I prefer grape over fruit punch. I hope to try this in recipes like I do with my regular whey. I think this mixed in yogurt would taste really good. Hope this review was helpful!

review_title: One of the best tasting protein powders out there
review_text:
I have tried many - now more than a dozen - different brands of protein powder over the last ten years. Vanilla Isopure Zero was my first, purchased in a GNC in a mall. It remains my favorite in terms of flavor - it isn't too sweet, it doesn't have that protein bitterness, it has a nice, smooth consistency, there's minimal gastrointestinal distress, and for some reason it doesn't tend to leave an unpleasant odor in my shaker cup after washing. The chocolate is okay, but the vanilla is where it is at, and the zero calories means that late-night workouts don't leave me going to bed feeling full.

It is more expensive than the majority of other powders out there, in terms of protein per dollar, which is why I rarely buy it. It also is no better or worse than other powders in supporting a workout; for someone like me, who only really maintains mass instead of building it, the extra protein is just there for support and recovery from strenuous hikes, not gains. I take the standard 5g/creatine a day, so creatine content is irrelevant to me anyway. So if flavor and consistency aren't a big deal, or you are fine with your experience with other powders, then there is no real reason to get this one.

However, I still recommend it, at least once.

Let's start with what I like about this product. The active ingredients are L-Tryptophan, L-theanine and GABA. I've always had trouble sleeping and all of those ingredients I've found to help without making me feel like I'm in a fog the next day. Plus this has actually effective doses and it really has helped with falling asleep in a nice relaxing way. But the taste...
I tried adding it to 6-8oz of water and it was very bitter. I've got a pretty good tolerance for chugging down things that are less than delicious from years of athletics and weight lifting and seriously this one was rough. Next night I tried 14-16oz of water and it wasn't bad, especially if you like the flavor of lavender. Though, that's a lot for some people to drink right before bed. So, if you can manage that or just really love bitter things, this product really does work well.

review_title: Don't write reviews very often, but had to for this!
review_text:
As a fitness coach, health and wellness enthusiast; I'm always looking for easy snacks / meals but healthy and not a bunch of fillers and processed. But above all, it's gotta taste good. Most of the time with "protein bars" I consistently find them to taste like chalk, or dry, and just lacking of flavor. There have been a few out there that are setting the bar up higher than before, but those brands are few and far between. And most of the time, they can get old just after a few weeks of having for a snack.

For me, this brand's Peanut Butter Candy has been one of the few protein focused snacks that I have consistently bought and will have almost every day. It literally taste like a peanut butter fudge bar you'd buy at some local artisan shop or a festival / farmers market. It's seriously that good. It's soft without being sticky and too artificial, but the candy bits provide a crunch to satisfy that mouth-feel factor. I really could not praise Jacked Factory any more, and would give this thing 6 stars or more if I could. They have stumbled across something here with this bar. It does not taste like a health bar at all, whatsoever. And the macros are pretty spot on.

You could argue it's a little higher on the calorie side, but if you check out the ingredients, there's no garbage like you'd find in a snickers or pack of M&Ms. Hands down, highly recommend this bar, and especially if you're a fan of Peanut Butter and Chocolate combo things. Get it now! I just ask, please Jack Factory, don't ever stop making this bar!

PROS

1. This vegan protein powder consists of pea and rice protein fermented by shiitake mushroom mycelia. Its protein digestibility-corrected amino acid score (PDCAAS) is the highest possible score of 1.0. (See below.)
2. It blends well into liquid, without any lumps, using a wire whisk.
3. It contains no sugar. It is sweetened with stevia.
4. It has a mild, inoffensive taste that is bearable to drink when blended into plain water. It is flavored with cocoa powder and stevia to offset the taste of the pea and rice protein.
5. There is a money-back guarantee for up to 60 days, which is offered stress-free, directly through Amazon.

CONS

1. This protein powder comes in a container made of thick plastic. Regardless of the claim of the plastic being a recyclable type, less than 9% of plastic generated in the US is actually recycled. There is no good reason why this product could not be packaged in a biodegradable, resealable Kraft bag instead of a plastic container.
2. There are far too many unspecified “natural flavorings” in this product. What are they? Who knows?
3. There is no information as to the source of the “pea and rice protein fermented by shiitake mycelia.” Given that this is crucial information for the consumer, I am greatly surprised at this oversight, given the good reputation of its most likely manufacturer. My findings on that probable manufacturer are included below.
4. All vegan protein powder is expensive, but this brand is especially pricey.

Premiere Manufacturer Using Mushrooms to Unlock the Full Potential of Plant-Based Proteins

The manufacturer of the main protein ingredient in this product is most likely Myco Technology (MT), a US corporation located in Aurora, Colorado. According to Dun & Bradstreet, MT was established and incorporated eight years ago, in 2013. MT has 100 total employees and currently generates $13.13 million annually in sales (USD). It originally received venture-capital startup funds in the amount of $82.6 million from Kellogg’s, Tyson Foods, and Müller (the largest milk supplier in UK), all of which have utilized its specialized plant-based-protein technology for their growing product lines of plant-based meat and dairy analogues. However, they are not the only companies that MT sells their specialized plant protein to.

The trademarked technology MT uses is called FermentIQ™. This process involves fermenting pea and rice protein with shiitake mushroom mycelium in order to improve their taste and aroma (which is pretty ghastly on its own), increase their ability to dissolve in liquid, and enhance the degree of viable protein in them. Because of the special way the pea and rice protein are fermented with mushroom mycelium, their “protein digestibility-corrected amino acid score” (PDCAAS) achieves the highest possible score of 1.0. PDCAAS is a method of evaluating the quality of a protein based on both the amino acid requirements of humans and their ability to digest it. (Note: This rating was adopted by the US FDA and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations/World Health Organization in 1993 as the “preferred best'" method to determine protein quality.)

MT has also developed a process called ClearIQ™, which is an organic bitterness blocker, which makes it possible for food and beverage manufacturers to utilizes far less sugar, salt, fat and other flavorings to mask bad tastes that naturally occur in various processed-food ingredients—especially pea and rice protein. It is very likely that this process has been utilized as well on the pea and rice protein powder included in this product.

This is a good pre-workout and contains all the ingredients I typically look for in a pre-workout that give me a mental and physical lift, as well as that "pump" feeling: caffeine, beta-alanine, creatine, and citrulline.

It also adds some dextrose, which is a fast-dissolving carbohydrate. I am not sure of the point of this, since once you burn 5 calories, you will have already used up the dextrose in one scoop (and I am on a low carb diet anyway and don't need that).

There is also some added Taurine, which is good because its inclusion gets rid of certain potential negative impacts of the amino acid beta-alanine in the body. Finally, there is some vitamin B12 included, but be aware it's not very much.

The taste is good and strong, which I like.

Overall, this is a good pre-workout. The name is kind of silly and an attempt to be edgy, but that's pretty much every pre-workout these days.

review_text:
I love this product for many reasons, not the least of which is the importance of supporting small businesses, especially one that has a big heart and a big mission.
But let's talk about the rice powder itself. The taste is exactly what you expect, it has the slightly nutty taste of brown rice. You can sprinkle a little bit in yogurt or on cereal, because, as you probably know, a hit of protein in the morning is very important. For me it's very important because that protein in the morning helps to stabilize blood sugar.
I know a lot of people will be using this in smoothies, but personally, I've really been enjoying it as an additive to foods and even cooking with it. When baking bread using a bannaton, I dust the wicker basket with a mixture of this powder and some ground white rice. It gives such a lovely texture and color to artisan breads that have raised in the basket. It's also good adding a few tablespoons to the bread itself. Even quick breads such as banana bread benefit from a tablespoon of this.
When you open the bag, it smells very fresh. Nothing worse than rancid rice. And speaking of such things, keep in mind that because it has been milled down to a powder, it's not going to keep us long as whole rice.
Not going to be a problem in our household, since I love putting this nearly everything!

review_text:
I ended up using it once and it is languishing in my cabinet. I was going to toss it but my husband wants to try it. Being who he is, that day may never come and I will throw it away, he being none the wiser.

First, the initial tentative taste. Wet finger, stick in powder, stick finger in mouth to taste. Then spit and spit into sink and flail for something, ANYTHING, to drink to wash out the taste. Even the mouthful of cold, leftover coffee from that morning was a huge improvement.

As a kid, did you ever eat mud, either by accident or on purpose? That. That is what the powder was like. Not a hint of a good flavor, not a hint of even a bitter, unsweetened cocoa for the “chocolate” flavor. Mud, gritty, nasty mud.

But maybe in a smoothie - milk, powder, a little sugar or honey, vanilla yogurt and a little ice to make it like a milkshake. Sweetened dirt in milk. So. I tried to hide it in a real milkshake, which obviously no one who bought this whey protein for their healthy diet regimen, is going to drink much of - a little real milk, the recommended scoops of powder, a lot of Breyers natural vanilla (or any kind of ice cream or brand), a couple squirts of chocolate syrup or powder (Nestle Quik, Ovaltine, etc) and a spin in the blender on the “shake” setting.

Almost ruined chocolate milkshakes for me. The chocolate syrup or Quik did little to hide the dirt flavor and grit.
