review_title: Low-carb flour- great for crackers, pizza crusts, soft tortillas, pita breads, biscuits..
review_text:
I've used 2 different organic pumpkin seed flours on Amazon.. this one and one other..
Differences I noticed is: the other brand said it was a 'product of China' while this brand said they are made from pumpkin seeds 'native to Central America' .. also this brand said that they use an 'age-old cold-pressing process' to naturally remove some of the seeds oil thus concentrating the protein.. the other brand didn't mention doing that. There is a difference price wise also with this one costing more than the other when u compare the amount you receive for the price.

We bought this for my husband who has been doing a low-carb keto diet ... this pumpkin seed flour has very low carbs (when u subtract the fiber)!! So we have used this to make crackers, pizza crusts, soft tortillas, pita breads and biscuits!! .. He loves it and can eat and not feel like he's missing out .. I will share our cracker recipe for anyone who wants to try it. We've also used other low carb flour (like almond and peanut) but now that we've found pumpkin seed flour which is very low carbs he prefers it.. I do wish it cost less..

My Italian cracker recipe:
1/2 cup pumpkin seed flour
1 tbsp Italian seasoning
1 tsp garlic powder
1/2 tsp onion powder
1 tsp oregano seasoning
1/4 tsp sea salt or to desired taste
2 tbsp olive oil
2 'chia eggs'*

Directions:
Preheat oven to 350'.. Mix all dry ingredients thoroughly... I use a fork to make sure its pressed and mixed well.. then add olive oil and mix thoroughly until it looks crumbly. Next add the 'chia egg' mixing well.. it maybe slightly wet & sticky but that's ok. Put the doughty ball on parchment paper and add another sheet of parchment paper on top.. press down and then roll it out to your desired cracker thickness. Then cut into squares and possibly sprinkle a touch more sea salt if you like more salt. Bake 15-20 minutes or until crispy.. oven temps vary so check around 15 minutes to make sure not burning. Enjoy!! ;)

*chia egg- Mix 1 tbsp of ground chia seeds with 3 tablespoons of water. Since this recipe calls for 2 chia eggs u would mix 2 tbsp of ground chia seeds with 6 tbsp of water.

**also on a side note I've read online that pumpkin seeds are known to remove intestinal worms ...

I shared a pic of the low carb crackers & cheese biscuits that I make with this flour .. I will try to add my cheese biscuits recipe soon! :)

review_title: Great Tasting bar with a couple of caveats
review_text:
Kudos to Send for putting out a nearly completely organically sourced trail/post-workout bar. The ingredients are all great - it’s sweetened with deglet dates and dried cherries only, with added pea protein, almonds, hemp seeds, coconut, spinach powder, chia seeds, sunflower lecithin and even the powerhouse mushrooms, lions mane and cordyceps . (Turmeric too.) Send has formulated a nicely balanced flavor with a little added sea salt and dollop of pure tangy lemon oil.

So, what’s Not to like? As someone with sugar sensitivities, while I appreciate that these bars are only sweetened with naturally occurring fruit sugars, which are certainly much better for you than added sugars, I feel that 18gms per bar - even if derived from fruit sugar, is a bit much. I just don’t need my trail bars to be that sweet tasting, and for my tastes I would’ve preferred roughly half that amount.

There are also 32gms of carbs in each bar, while providing only 7 grams of protein. In my opinion these are not fantastic numbers. I personally would’ve preferred more protein and less carbs and sugar. The recommended ratio for post-workout recovery varies, but the general consensus seems to be in the 3-1 range (protein to carbs,) and if that’s an acceptable rule of thumb, these bars fall short of that ratio, as there would have to be only around 21gm carbs to 7gm protein to achieve that ratio. Of course that ratio varies depending on whether you're trying to lose weight (In which case the carb to protein ratio goes further down,) or whether you’re using them for some extra post workout energy.

If you’re not concerned with weight loss and aren't worried about sugar intake, these are a good choice in terms of a post-workout recovery snack, which is after all what they were designed for. They will definitely give you that quick energy infusion. They taste fabulous and are mostly organic, are gluten free and vegan.

(Note this is a 5 star product - I docked it one star because of the high fruit sugar content and carb/protein ratio)

review_text:
So . . . I wanted to get some kind of drink that would help me to start the day off right, and with 21g of protein, this tasty chocolate-flavored drink seemed to fit the bill. It's a plant-based protein drink with, believe it or not, ABSOLUTELY NO SUGAR, despite its slightly sweet taste. It is only slightly thick in texture.

I like this drink because it tastes good and I'm getting a lot of nutrition in a small bottle that I can grab quickly as I go out the door in the morning. Sometimes I'm not going anywhere at all, but simply want to get started on my day right away as soon as I get up. Sure, it would be nice if I scrambled myself an egg and fried a couple of strips of bacon to go with it. The reality is that if I didn't have something like this around, I'd probably grab the first pile of junk I could stuff down.

This is a richly chocolate-flavored drink with lots of healthy goodness -- 11 oz. of plant-based protein -- to help me start my day, and it's only 190 calories!!! If you're dieting, this would fit nicely into meal plans.

This package of 16 drinks for $51.99 breaks down to $3.25 per drink. I think it seems too pricey, but for someone who goes to Starbucks every morning for coffee, this might seem like a bargain. I wish I could afford it, but at roughly $100 for a one-month supply, it's way out of my price range.

I highly recommend it for it's flavor, texture and nutrition, but to me this drink seems overpriced.

review_title: BCAA capsules for half the price of Other Name brand
review_text:
I purchased OWN PWR BCAA (Branched Chain Amino Acid) 400 Capsules for the first time. I was using BCAAs by Other Name brand, but decided to give OWN PWR a shot due to the price difference. The main reason I switched to these was price. These are about half the price of the Other Name brand ($12.59 bs $24.29). The capsules are identically sized, the bottle is identical & the labels are identical when it comes to the ingredients & supplement facts. These are made for Amazon.

As there are no special dietary markings or logos & the capsules are gelatin, I’d guess they’re made from beef &/or pork, so would not be vegan, kosher or halal. This is not an issue for me. I do not notice any sort of taste when taking these. The serving suggestion is 2 capsules (1g of BCAA) before or after your workout. I take 4 capsules 40 mins before (sometimes closer to workouts), I’ll take 2 capsules during & 2-4 capsules after (depending how long I worked out for). When I ride my MTB, I’ll ride for 2-3 hours (30-45 miles) on trails/paths. For this I’ll take 4 capsules before, 2-4 capsules at the halfway mark & 2-4 capsules when the ride concludes. I know that’s a lot of capsules to swallow, but it’s convenient to carry & easy to take.

If your looking for BCAA capsules to supplement with, don’t mind taking a lot of capsules, OWN PWR BCAA Capsules a much less expensive option then the Other Name brand & because of that, I’d recommend them.

Thank you for taking the time to read my review, I hope it was helpful.

review_title: Pure Creatine Monohydrate, Perfect For Training
review_text:
It shouldn't be hard to get creatine wrong since it is a basic amino acid. However, it is often sold with fillers, other strange additives, and unnatural ingredients. Here, you have just pure, non-GMO (I don't know if it can be GMO, but at least appreciate they call it out), creatine monohydrate. No other fillers or additives.

I started taking creatine this year as a way to support my body in working out and recovery from distance running training. There are so many variables but I do feel like I've noticed some level of improvement in my endurance during training and recovery time.

According to the Mayo Clinic:
"Your body stores creatine as phosphocreatine primarily in your muscles, where it's used for energy. As a result, people take creatine orally to improve athletic performance and increase muscle mass.

People also use oral creatine to treat certain brain disorders, neuromuscular conditions, congestive heart failure and other conditions. Topical creatine might be used to treat aging skin."

This is nicely packaged (I much prefer the containers with lids to the bags). It also comes with a portion scoop inside. It is reasonably affordable with this being about a 4-month supply. So I'm very happy to have it part of my supplementation regimen.

review_title: Tastes like extremely watered down milk with no aftertaste.
review_text:
If you hate that terrible aftertaste of sweetener, and you don't love the flavour of milk, this is probably the best protein powder you will find.
I have recently gotten a promotion/raise and decided to finally try several different protein powders even though some of them don't have samples. The Isopure Infusions were the closest I had ever gotten before. If I threw a Crystal Lite in there, I could drink it after a run when I was extremely thirsty, and I would just barely taste the terrible artificial sweetener aftertaste.
But I am a supertaster, and that was not enough.
I wanted something that I could drown out with other flavours, especially something that I can cook (haven't tried this yet). Every single other protein powder I have tried has been a disappointment, except PEScience, which I think wasn't simply because it was the second to last one and my expectations had been trashed at that point. With PES, I did manage to drink the entire sample packet but I doubt I would drink more. I am going to try the other samples for baking, though.
I tried this with just water before doing my plan, which was to make a taro boba tea (I also tried that taro boba tea protein powder you can buy here. I did not like it at all.)
I LOVE taro boba tea, but it is full of sugar. If I could get this to work, then I could actually have a treat any day AND finally meet my protein macros (my Cals are low so powder is basically required)
Trying this with water I discovered that instead of tasting like spoiled milk with an aftertaste, it actually tasted more like water than like milk!?
I tried it in my boba tea and drank that down in an alarmingly fast rate of less than five minutes, y'all.
I would not drink this by itself, but in practically anything else, you can't really taste it.
Important note, though: that this is only true if I actually let it settle all the way down, which means I pre-prep this. If I attempt to mix it in something immediately after shaking it up, it tastes more milky and is quite foamy, which is probably tolerable for anyone who does not dislike the taste of plain milk/who likes milkshakes but is more difficult for me as a supertaster who does not like milkshakes.

I hope this helped anyone else who needs more protein and dislikes both milk and artificial sweeteners. I HAVE heard that batches vary and this is only my first one, though, so I will update if my next batch is less delicious.

Final Note: I was able to mix this with just a spoon the first time, but since then I have used my shaker bottle. If my bottle is still very hot from a recent washing, though, it can be difficult, so just be sure to temper this or make sure to mix it cold if heat is not necessary.

product_title: Garden of Life Organic Vegan Sport Protein Powder, Vanilla - Probiotics, BCAAs, 30g Plant Protein for Premium Post Workout Recovery - NSF Certified, Keto, Gluten & Dairy Free, Non GMO 19 Servings
review_text:
To start, I find it comical when people complain about the taste of plant based proteins. I mean what did they expect it to taste like - the skittles rainbow? If you want amazing flavored protein - then go buy brands that fill your protein full of sugars and other artificial flavors to get great tastes.

On the other hand, if you want a protein powder with clean organic ingredients then you’ve come to the right place for a review. I am personally a fitness nut and I’m always looking for brands to meet my diet needs.

No, the bottle doesn’t come full to the brim with protein powder - but it tells you how many servings you’re getting so stop acting surprised that the bottle is half full. Per your TWO scoops (yes some people don’t like the fact that it’s two scoops but it is), you get 30 grams of protein, your BCAAs, glutamine and probiotics. Your two scoops are roughly 7g of carbs and less than a gram of sugar. The recovery blend in this protein is fantastic as well (tart cherry, turmeric, etc.) - which is great for post recovery. I like that this company uses a blend of plant based proteins rather than just one protein like some other companies do (ex: pea protein (cheapest one you can use)).

Blend-ability/mixing: absolutely amazing.
I use this two ways: #1 I simply use 12 ounces of unsweetened almond milk and two scoops of powder. I typically mix it in a blender bottle with the little metal shaker ball and it mixes great. Yes it’s a bit chalky and has a bit of a funky taste/texture, but i find it very good overall for a plant based protein powder mixed with almond milk. #2 I mix this in my vita mix with unsweetened almond milk, a banana and peanut butter, or i change it up and do mixed berries and a tablespoon of tart cherry juice. Again, the texture/taste takes some getting used to but in my opinion it tastes great for a plant based powder.

NEXT - the gas/bloating/stomach discomfort topic. I’m lactose intolerant, I’ve had plenty of heartburn/GERD issues and many gas/bloating problems on various other whey/isolate proteins and some other plant based proteins brands. This brand hands down has not caused me ANY of these. I’ve had zero bloating - zero gas - zero stomach discomforts - and zero heartburn. I feel like the clean ingredients speak for themselves and it shows when your body responds positively to it.

Finally the heavy metal concerns people have about plant based proteins made with organic soils. I mean I can say this much - it’s organic and anything that comes from organic soil is okay in my book. I’d much rather use a product that has naturally occurring things in it than use protein blends that add god awful amounts of unknown garbage that is probably 100 times worse for you than some metals found in organic soil. Sure if you’re worried about it then research the brand and see if they provide stats about it but I’m frankly not that concerned about it. Go look at any major popular whey protein powder on the market and compare the amount of ingredients it has to a plant based protein. I bet you probably couldn’t even decipher what half the ingredients in the whey proteins are because it has so much fillers and other garbage.

Overall - this is a great protein power for those looking for a good post workout blend. Highly recommend it and I’ve been using them for quite some time.

review_text:
You open the can, excited to try out E G G W H I T E protein. It has incredible properties - more bioavailable than whey, tons of good amino acids, and better than any plant protein for stimulating muscle protein synthesis. The first thing you experience is the smell. The stench of old eggs wafts up from the tin. The powder is fine and dusty - as you disturb the jug, a small cloud escapes into the air.

"I have a strong stomach and a resilient taste. I can do this," you whisper to yourself, not entirely sure. The macros on the label are pretty compelling - only 1g of carbs for 16g of protein - that's unheard of. You pour the recommended amounts into your shaker bottle, and shake. The mixture immediately forms a foam that refuses to settle out. It's been Activated, and it hungers for blood.

You try to take a sip. The foam is overwhelming. The scent of bad eggs is replaced by the taste of bad eggs. "Maybe if I get to the liquid under the foam, it will be better," you hope. The bottle goes up, and up, and up, and finally you feel the liquid enter your mouth. Your tongue recoils in horror - the taste is far worse than the smell. The cup goes down. "Maybe I can mix this with something?" you think with a tone of despair. No. You cannot mix this with something. Nothing tames the foam, and the underlying rotten egg flavor dominates all attempts to cover it up.

Resignation fills your head. You start googling "Can I compost protein powder?" and "Ethics of donating nasty food."

review_text:
I’m a fan of other Nugenix products namely the ZMA and that’s why I tried this GH boost. I didn’t read the negative reviews for this before I tried it but I wish I had. I’ve been a “natural” bodybuilder for over 35 years and I’ve never taken a supplement that will literally take your breath away. If someone is prone to panic attacks or has anxiety this product could cost them a trip to the hospital. The reaction I had after drinking it was that dramatic. Fortunately I wasn’t driving but could go chill out in a chair until it passed.
At first there’s a rush of warmth and tingling to the head and neck. Similar to what you would get from beta-alanine but much more intense. This booster doesn’t contain BA so I’m not sure where this sensation comes from. Within 30 seconds I was short of breath and in about a minute I was struggling to actually catch my breath. This lasted about 20-30 minutes for each of the 4 nights that I took it. Within 3 days I started feeling like I was coming down with a cold or flu and since there’s a pretty high rate of them in my area I figured that’s what it was. The headaches were increasingly worse to the point that on the 4th day I was skipping sets during my workout. My partner said that in the couple of years we’ve trained together he’s never seen me skipping sets. I decided to dx the booster and the very next day the flu like symptoms and especially the headaches went away.
If this product works for you then great but it’s definitely not for me. It appears to have good marketing and even includes a comment about how it’s inspected by the FDA. I’m a bit skeptical about this claim because it’s unlikely the US FDA would allow a product onto the market that could potentially harm someone.

review_text:
I love a good pre-workout. Now that I am typically burning 1000+ calories, 5-6 times a week, from lifting and the StairMaster or rowing machines, I do benefit from a good pre-workout. I look for certain things in a pre-workout, namely caffeine, beta-alanine, creatine, and citrulline. This formula doesn't contain creatine, but nonetheless has a lot of other ingredients that will make up for this. Plus, some people don't want to take creatine for various reasons.

It also contains plenty of nitric-oxide raising substances, including citrulline and red spinach extract (which, like beet root, contains plenty of nitrates). And, I like that it has taurine in it, because not only does it give me a mental lift, but it is necessary with any supplement that has beta-alanine in it, for balance purposes.

It also contains plenty of choline-based chemicals, which provide a good mental lift. And, the taste is pretty decent as well, without the need for dumb fillers like maltodextrin. I wish it wasn't Splenda (sucralose) based, and I prefer stevia, but that is hard to find in pre-workouts.

Overall, this is a nice pre-workout!

review_title: Looks all wrong but tastes delicious to me and it’s like a meal
review_text:
This review is for the Lorissa’s Kitchen Whole-Made Medley Sweet Barbecue Bars.

There are 12 1.5 ounce 190 calorie bars in this package and these bars are made of wholesome ingredients. Each bar is 190 calories. The idea of combining grass-fed beef with seeds seems weird. The resulting bar looks weird as if it were a fig newton but without the pastry.

INGREDIENTS:
- pumpkin seeds
- dried apples
- peanuts
- finely chopped beef jerky
- dried egg whites
- almond butter and peanut butter with BBQ seasoning

In summary, I love these. These are wholesome bars, taste great, and it feels like I am eating a meal. However, who would have thought this combination of ingredients is even possible? It is that weirdness that causes me to rate this 4 stars. However, the taste to me is 5 stars.

UPDATE - I gave a bar to my postman and he thought this was good. He gives this four stars.

UPDATE 2/8/20 - I also gave one bar to my boyfriend and he really liked them as well. He gave it four stars only because he said the bar was too thick for his teeth.

This is a solid 4-star bar based on my research with two people I know. I do have a girlfriend who refused to try this because she said it sounded unappetizing to her.

review_title: really shines when used w/ a frother- makes it creamy and foamy. Nice flavor. Quite sweet
review_text:
It IS smooth and creamy. I get the best creaminess when I blend it with a [[ASIN:B0BBV3SLZH handheld frother like this]]. The bag doesnt specifically say creamer, and since it is a coconut powder base, --and in y experience--I wouldn't expect it to lighten coffee as much as dairy creamer. However, it can lighten it a little with a frother. Yet, if you just want it as an additive and not concerned with creaming, then know that it dissolves well with a simple stir of a spoon.

As for taste, that will come down to personal preference and perception. I am not usually impressed with flavored powders, but this is actually pleasant tasting to me. I could tell that it is "white chocolate raspberry" upon sniffing the open bag. The taste is the same. It's pretty good (to me!). Nice when I want something a little different. I have also tried it in a cup of hot cocoa with success.

Says to use 1 scoop in 6-8 ounces of coffee. I concur. I initially tried in a 4 ounce brew of espresso and that was way too sweet, but doable. Was much better in an 8-10 ounce cup.

It is quite sweet, less so when used in more liquid. Why do these products always overload with the sweetness?

Says that this container has "about 30 servings". Currently priced at $43.99 making this at best $1.47 per serving.

Is it worth it? I dont rate on price, but the LOW amount of collagen (4 grams) and MCT (1.5 grams) makes this a pricy boutique level product that doesn't offer enough of anything to make this a repurchase for me.

But the ingredients are good AND they have all these details in the product description, so it is easy enough to make an informed decision. Hence, I probably would not have ordered this had I been shopping around.

In short: taste is pretty good (can tell it is white chocolate raspberry), little sweeter than I prefer, mixes well with spoon, really shines when used with frother, nice way to get additional collagen but I wouldnt rely on it as my only source unless you are looking for low amount with a little MCT. 4 stars

review_title: collagen peptides from grass fed cows, nothing added. Just basic, good quality product
review_text:
Currently $32.99 for over a pound (17.64 ounces) of collagen peptides powder. That price falls well within range for the weight, as well as the amount of collagen per serving. Many fall within the 8-15 grams range, and the serving size for this provides 20 grams. Currently costs less than Vital Proteins.

20 grams (18 grams protein). That can easily be halved depending on your needs. You decide what is best for you. I normally stick to around 10-12 grams per serving as there is only so much protein the body can utilize at once, and 10-12 grams seems to be sweet spot for me. If I want more, then I have another serving later in day. That being said, if taking the 20 gram serving, then expect about 25 servings per container. Even if it were 3x as much, or half as much, I simply dont rate on price.

They do a good job of showing exactly what is in this, how much, where it is from, amino acid profile, etc. Really nothing missing. Except why they call it "enhanced". It originally caught my attention because I thought maybe it was collagen peptides WITH something else. I really like when it includes vitamin c, hyaluronic acid.. basically supplements that enhance absorption. But nothing here. It is just bovine collagen peptides. Grass fed (remember when grass fed was hard to come by?). And so.. the name is just the name. The only time when it may have been relevant is before collagen peptides really became a thing. Before "peptides" (aka "hydrolyzed"--you early adopter remember that term? haha), there was just collagen or "gelatin". Which is collagen in pure form, and often used to gel up food stuffs. Then "hydrolyzed" entered the scene, which basically takes collagen gelatin, and breaks it down further into a much more easily digestible and easily absorbed form. At some point, hydrolyzed was replaced with peptides. Easier to remember and spell, I suppose. Anway, in that sense the collagen gelatin would have been "enhanced" into a much better (and pricier) form. But that was 10-15 years ago. Today? enhanced would indicated the addition of something. And there isnt anything here.

I am amused that they have the term hydrolyzed in use, with "peptides" in parenthesis. I may be onto something!

Yet, I dont down rate on that. I want to, but it is just a name. And I can clearly see all that is in it with quick glance of the pictures, which is what I would normally do when shopping. I was still curious though, so I gave it a try.

5 stars. NOT because it is better than other, but because it meets expectations of a good, effective, collagen peptide powder. How much you use, and how much you want to pay is personal.

I got this to try as part of my own sports drink for continuing energy through my workouts. I found it was tasteless in water, thickened it a bit, and about 98% dissolved in water. While that does leave a hint of graininess, I let the liquid settle, then gently pour it into a cup so that the few undissolved grains of powder stay in the first glass, and voila.

It doesn't change the flavor of anything I add to the Maltodextrin and water, which works out pretty well.

Please note that if you try to add a LOT of the powder to water or other liquid, it won't dissolve as fully, but that's the case with a lot of powders. Once the water becomes more saturated, less of whatever you add to it will dissolve as quickly or fully.

If you're looking for a rather fast carb to add to workouts or if you do labor all day and want to carry a hydrating drink with some carbs and calories, Judee's Maltodextrin Powder could come in very handy. For extended runs, workouts or labor, adding some protein could help.

review_text:
So the first thing you'll notice when you start to add this to your coffee or whatever drink of choice is how bitter it is. But over time your pallet adjusts. I started with 1/4th of a plastic measuring spoon that's in the bag, now I'm at almost a full spoon. This is what I drink every other morning:

Light roast organic coffee with soy milk or Lactose Free milk. If you use other milks the amount below might need to change, mix stuff in and spoon taste before calling it done.

1/4-1 tiny spoon (measuring spoon that comes with it) of OM Mushroom mix.
1/2 Tsp of Vanilla extract (for sweetness to mask the bitter mushroom flavor)
1/4-1/2 Tsp of Turmeric (yup the yellow one you use for cooking). Over time this too increases from 1/4 to 1/2 Tsp - it's an anti-inflammatory
1/4 Tsp of Pumpkin spice or cinnamon (if you have a spice shaker just shake in 3-4 good shakes

Whatever else you want to add to your coffee.

Experiment but remember, if you put in too much and it's bitter, just lower the amount and increase it bi-weekly, your pallet over time won't taste the bitter mushrooms and then you can add more.

P.S.
I see people commenting about an expiration date vs. BUBD - best used by date. Expiration date is recommended by the seller, BUBD is the last date the product should be used so you technically can go up until BUBD date but if your expiration date has expired before you received the product, it's something to definitely take up with a seller. I highly recommend getting Prime Amazon Account, with things like that I have never had issues returning or exchanging. Do not recommend keeping expired chocolate but BUBD as long as you keep the bag in cool, dry place is your ultimate expiration date.

review_title: This product is very likely contaminated with hexane since it is not USDA Certified Organic
review_text:
Ingredients: Sunflower seeds

PROS

1. Mild, inoffensive taste.
2. Fine powder that blends well with a wire whisk.
3. No additives, only sunflower seeds.
4. Vegan.
5. Conveniently packaged in a small, plastic bag, rather than a thick, plastic jar. Unfortunately, neither a bag nor a jar is realistically going to be recycled in the USA—whether they are labeled “recyclable” or not, the options for recycling plastic are extremely limited since China stopped allowing the US to dump all its plastic waste on them. However, those thick plastic jars are far worse than bags like this, because they contain a lot more plastic.

CONS

1. This product is not organic, and there is zero statement from the manufacturer that this protein powder is hexane free. I have included below information on how sunflower seed protein powder is manufactured, for anyone who might be interested. Sunflower is not a type of protein powder that is safe to consume, for conscientious consumers who wish to avoid hexane, unless it is USDA Certified Organic.

OILSEED EXTRACTION

Hexane is used widely in the industrial extraction of oil from plant sources. This process produces two marketable food products: oil and a high-protein powder residue. In the USA, this protein powder is primarily used for animal feed, with a relatively small proportion of it sold for human consumption in the health food market. While some other countries set legal limits of hexane residues in food products, regrettably, the US Food and Drug Administration (USDA) does not require that US food manufacturers test their food products for hexane residue, unless it is officially verified as USDA Certified Organic.

The Typical Manufacturing Process for Non-Organic, Solvent Extraction of Plant Proteins

1. Examples of edible oilseeds (nuts and legumes are also seeds) include: almonds, borage, canola/rapeseed, corn, cottonseed, flax (AKA linseed), grapeseed, hazelnut, hemp, macadamia, Moringa oleifera, peanut, pepitas (pumpkin seed), pine seed, safflower, sesame, soybean, sunflower, and walnuts. Examples of oil fruits include: avocado, palm fruits (coconut, African oil palm AKA Elaeis guineensis), and olive. Examples of microalgae used for edible oil production include: Chlorella sorokiniana, Chlorella vulagaris, and Nannochloropsis.
2. Oilseeds, leaves, or dried algae are cracked, flaked, ground to powder, then pressed. Mechanical extraction is called "crushing" or "cold pressing." The types of mechanical extraction include: expeller-press, screw-press, ram-press, and ghani (a type of powered mortar and pestle employed in India).
3. Commercial oil extraction for oils and protein powders which are not USDA Certified Organic is typically accomplished by using the petroleum-derived chemical solvent, hexane, because it removes a lot more oil, is quicker, and cheaper than utilizing mechanical extraction alone. The ground powders are heated, soaked with hexane, shaken, and then pressed. Together the heat and hexane break down the powders and cause them to release more oil than they would otherwise do without those interventions.
4. After pressing the hexane-processed powder to extract oil, the hexane is separated from the oil, not because manufacturers really care if it is in the food, but to save money, because if it is recovered, it can be reused many times. The hexane is separated from the oil via distillation. The hexane-infused oil is heated to 300° F (149° C). Since hexane’s boiling point is 69° C, this temperature causes the hexane to evaporate. Its vapor is captured in the distiller’s coils, condensed, and collected. Unfortunately, during the extraction and recovery processes, inevitably, toxic fumes of hexane are released into the air. The immediate danger this causes is the poisoning of unprotected factory workers. Scientific studies have revealed that, when inhaled, hexane can cause damage to the nervous system throughout the body because of its solubility in neural lipids (i.e. it accumulates in body fat). There is also environmental danger, because hexane reacts with pollutants in the air to form ground-level ozone. Inhaling ozone damages the lungs. In terms of global warming, ground-level ozone interferes with the photosynthesis process of plants, reducing the amount of CO2 they can remove from the air—and rising levels of CO2 contribute to global warming. On a dietary level, in spite of the manufacturer’s attempts to remove hexane from the extracted oil, it unavoidably contains varying amounts of residual hexane, which no manufacturer is required by law to test for and report on to anyone, especially consumers. Research has shown that animals fed with hexane-extracted, oilseed protein powder can experience hexane toxicity. There is no reason to believe humans would not experience the same toxicity from consuming those same hexane-extracted oils or protein powders on a regular basis, since all oilseed protein powders come from the same manufacturing plants, whether they end up being eaten by farm animals or people.

Alternatives to Hexane

Non-toxic alternatives to hexane have been well known to the scientific community since the early 1970’s, and possibilities have only grown for their use over time. Some of these options include: (1) Aqueous enzymatic extraction (AEE) AKA water-assisted enzymatic extraction, which utilizes enzymes such as cellulase, pectinase, hemicellulase and protease; (2) supercritical carbon dioxide; (3) terpenes such as d-limonene (derived from citrus peels), p-cymene (derived from tree oils), and α-pinene (derived from pine trees), (4) ionic liquids (non-aqueous salt solutions).

review_text:
What do you get when you stuff 10 pound into a 5 pound sack? Now imagine doing that with a protein shake. It's actually kinda crazy how much protein is stuffed into each bottle. 40 grams! This compares with a typical 20-25g in a bottle this size. So what is the end result?

If you can get past the consistency, which isn't really a problem for me, the flavor is just OK. There is some real cocoa notes there but also a somewhat bitter artificial sweetener aftertaste. Truthfully, it tastes about how I would expect an artificially sweetened protein shake to taste.

Finally, this isn't fortified unlike other supplement or protein drinks. Compared to a similar sized Premier Protein shake, this has some calcium but that's about it where the Premier drink has 24 vitamins and mineral (and 30g of protein). You're here for the massive amount of protein in this drink.

In summary, this is really geared to athletes that are looking for very high and concentrated levels of protein. they aren't worried about full meal replacement or vitamin/mineral fortification. If that's you and don't mind a very thick shake or the taste of artificial sweetener, then this is definitely a drink to consider. For others looking to get a more balanced, sweeter, or easier to drink shake, I would look elsewhere.

review_text:
I have been using Legion's products for a while (mostly Pulse and Recharge), but I had never ventured into buying their Whey Protein. I had been using other products, but finally decided to test it out.

All of Legion's items are high quality products you can trust. In the past, I have tried different flavors, but I really wanted to get unflavored whey protein powder so that I could decide to flavor my shake however I wanted to without an overpowering flavor. Besides the fact that it is non-GMO and hormone/antibiotic free, it is from grass-fed cows. What I also liked about the ingredients of the protein powder is that there are no added sugars and only 1g of total sugars, whereas others protein powders I have used in the past have had anywhere from 1.5g - 2g sugar per serving. There is also 25g of whey protein isolate per serving, which is pretty good. Also, when you compare calories, this was also the lower in caloric intake by 10-20%.

When I first opened the bottle, I was surprised to see that it was only 60-70% full. It was really strange; seemed like a waste of money on the packaging. Why not make the bottle smaller? Then, I looked at the net weight on the packaging. It was only 1.75 lbs, whereas it had been advertised as 2 lb. Guess they decided to round up. I looked at Legion's other flavors and realized that some of Legion's protein powders are 2 lb and others are only 1.75 lb. Not sure why they felt they needed to reduce the quantity of this one by 12%. Not a huge deal, but if you are comparing costs between this protein powder and others, take note on the amount of protein powder you are actually buying.

I tried this mixed with water and also with some almond milk. In both cases, it mixed in with the liquid pretty easily. With the water, there was a subtle taste, but not too noticeable. When mixed with almond milk, I can barely perceive a difference in the taste.

Overall, good quality product with good amount of protein and without an overpowering flavor.

There are a few things I look for in a protein supplement. The first of course is value. This has one of the best bang for buck protein supplements out there. Another is the use of sunflower lecithin over soy lecithin. Lecithin just makes sure it stays a powder, and helps maintain the flavor of the protein, and this product uses my ingredient of choice. I personally prefer "Supplement Facts" labeling as opposed to "Nutrition Facts" labeling when it comes to protein powders but it's not a deal breaker for me. So this brand hits some major brownie points.
The flavor is pretty good. It's not outstanding, but it's not bad. I'd say it leans above average when it comes to flavor. I'm going to a pet peeve when it comes to reviews... This company uses maltodextrin, and sucralose. Sucralose is a sugar substitute, and maltodextrin is used to help maintain the flavor. So of course protein powders will have better flavor when these are added. You can't have great flavor and no sweeteners or additives at the same time. For this supplement, you get a good flavor with very minimum use of sweeteners and a flavor preservative. If you have an over-all healthy diet, this will fall completely in line.
So over-all, very pleased with this product, and will constantly renew this purchase if the price point stays within range.

[Background... doesn't have to do with product specifics, skip this paragraph if desired] I have tried tons of protein powders over the years and struggled to find very many that I like. Like a few other reviewers, I was a fan of the cherry Protein2O bottled beverages, but couldn't justify the cost-to-protein ratio (plus I wanted a powder anyway) so I gave this a try.

I was impressed with the smoothness of this powder. As advertised, it mixes nearly as thin as plain water unlike some of the other protein powders I have tried. It does froth up a lot when mixing though so make sure you leave enough air space in your shaker bottle to account for this. Definitely let it sit for a couple minutes after mixing for the froth to settle. The taste is quite good, fairly sweet if that's your thing, but it is definitely something that I could drink and enjoy regularly.

The only real downside is the cost. For roughly $25 you get 20 servings, each serving having 20g of protein equal to a total of 400g of protein. Ideally I like my shakes to have closer to 30 grams of protein per serving, but that's an easy solution here of just using 1.5 scoops. The problem with this is that my existing brand provides bags for a similar price but a total of 1200g of protein (also with relatively clean ingredients), so this powder ends up being 3x as expensive. It's nice to have around for a change of flavor, but I can't justify making it my daily driver protein powder based on that price. If you're in a place where the price works for you, I highly recommend giving it a try.

review_title: Tastes Good, A Whole Lotta Shaking Going On
review_text:
To sum this up, it's good tasting protein powder. Very convenient pouch. Requires a lot of shaking.

The most important thing about any protein powder to me is taste. This stuff actual tastes good. I used fat free milk. If it was just a bag I used on my own it would be 5 stars for the powder alone. But it's not, it's in a portable travel bag.

Your first challenge when using this is pouring your liquid 'of choice' into the bag. If you're out somewhere and using a water bottle or milk carton with a small head, it may be easier. If you're using a wide mouth bottle good luck. You'll need to get your liquid stream just perfect to hit the hole. I ended up using a small funnel (not provided).

Once you've found a way to fill to the fill line using whatever method works best for you, then comes the shaking.

Inside the bag there's a small plastic mixer ball, I was really looking forward to that ball doing some work like in a mixing bottle.

After 5 minutes of shaking, (workout suggestion, add wrist weights to your arms while shaking, it'll be like using a shake weight) taking a sip the taste was good, then the powder lump came, more shaking. I think I shook that bag for 10 minutes. That mixer ball seemed to want to hang out towards the top out of the mix, seemed pretty useless inside.

It still wasn't perfectly mixed, so I'm taking off a star for the functionality of the bag.

I'm not sure what I could have done better, I kept reading the directions, hoping there'd be some sort of shaking advice. It just says shake. No mention of shake till you can no longer shake. Then shake more.

Over all, for protein powder on the go this isn't bad. If I'm on an airplane and decide to entertain myself while upsetting the people around me with the shaking it would be perfect. If I'm driving a long distance and need an arm workout this could help. If I'm home, I think I'd rather use a real shaker bottle.

So, the taste is good, the implementation is what I question. You may find that you enjoy a lump of protein powder more than I do.

I hope your found this review helpful.

review_title: This is what we get from a product named "Blackmarket"
review_text:
When I review powders like this, I look at both how honest they are about their ingredients and how it tastes.

Unfortunately, this product does its very best to NOT tell you what's in it. The ingredients are microscopic and almost impossible to read. In fact, the only way I could read what's in it is online. Broadly, its ingredients can be grouped as the following:

INCREASE ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE
* Citrulline Malate: Enhances athletic anaerobic performance and relieves muscle soreness.
* Beta-Alanine: Aids in the production of carnosine (a compound that affects muscle endurance in high-intensity exercise).
* Betaine Anhydrous: Reduces blood homocysteine levels to improve athletic performance.
* Choline Bitartrate: Increases athletic performance.
* Alpha GPC 50%: Improves thinking skills (this one is weird, I guess it's to make you feel better for taking it?)

ABSORPTION
* AstraGin: Facilitates absorption of nutrients.

CAFFEINE
* Cafe Alatus: Caffeine, derived from green coffee.

The third one is the most important, and the secret to all these powders is the caffeine. They can dress it up however they want (and often do), but caffeine is what's going to give you that pumped feeling. I don't drink coffee, so this is how I get my caffeine, and I mix it into my shake. I used about half of what the scoop provides. You won't find this on the product, but it's in the above infographic:
* 1/2 scoop: 75 mg of caffeine
* 1 scoop: 150 mg of caffeine
* 2 scoops: 300 mg of caffeine

Your average cup of coffee is 95 mg, so one scoop is essentially a little less than two cups in a dose. Two scoops would put you at over three cups of coffee. The Mayo Clinic recommends no more than 400 mg daily, so unless you're planning to drink nothing else with caffeine for the rest of the day, going that high with two scoops isn't recommended.

I do appreciate that the powder isn't flavored to look red (so that we think it tastes like watermelon, we're not 12). The flavoring unfortunately tastes rather artificial. It's palatable, but I can't imagine drinking it in water without any other flavors to offset it.

I wish the powder had more transparency, but then, expectations are low for a product titled "Blackmarket."

review_title: A protein powder like none I've ever tried before
review_text:
I was skeptical of how this would taste just based on the fact that marshmallow cereal pieces and protein powder are not something I've ever seen combined before, but it honestly works somewhat well!

The charms seem identical to those out of your typical cereals with marshmallows in them, and the protein powder base that they are mixed in to seems be a standard vanilla flavor. The vanilla flavor itself isn't amazing (but I've also never been a fan of vanilla protein powders so take that with a grain of salt). The flavor really comes out as the marshmallows start to dissolve and you get the sweetness and flavor of the marshmallow mixing with the vanilla.

One thing that is still a bit weird to me is taking a drink and feeling a clump of something in my mouth. Typically with protein powder it's a chunk of undissolved protein powder and is gross, but in this case it's a pleasant surprise of a nice sweet marshmallow! The protein powder itself in this product dissolves well and I have not had an issues with clumps of undissolved powder.

The ingredients here seem fairly clean which is good, not a ton of additives. The artificial sweetener is sucralose which I know a few people who have issues with so just something to note. The marshmallows provide a small amount of added sugar as well (2.5g added sugar, 4g total sugar) which was less than I expected.

I was pleasantly surprised by this protein powder. If you're someone who likes vanilla protein powders and wants to spice things up a bit, this protein powder with marshmallows mixed in is definitely worth a try!

Other companies do produce other creatine's that taste better and mix better with water, but that is because they are putting things besides creatine in them. Pure simple creatine won't mix well. Also, STICK to the recommended 5 grams. Creatine is very safe, actually, Creatine is something that your body naturally produces. HOWEVER if you are taking a large amount of it over an extended period of time, you can cause damage to your liver. You don't need much, 5 grams is enough. It doesn't matter when you take it as far as your workout is concerned, just take it consistently every day. Make sure you are hydrated when you start creatine, if you are dehydrated you will leave yourself susceptible to cramping.

review_title: Mild tasting, vegan protein powder contains only 1 organic ingredient
review_text:
Ingredients: Pea protein isolate, organic hemp protein, alkalized cocoa powder, Sacha Inchi protein, natural flavor, milled chia seed, stevia leaf extract, salt, guar gum, spirulina, kelp powder, dulse powder.

This 1-pound container of protein powder offers 15 servings or 20 grams of protein each.

The 30-gram scoop that comes with this product holds 4 tablespoons (1/4 cup) of this protein powder.

PROS

1. This vegan protein powder blends well, without any lumps, just by using a wire whisk.
2. It has a mild, inoffensive taste that is bearable to drink when blended into plain water. It is flavored with cocoa powder and stevia to offset the taste of the various ingredients that don’t taste very good on their own, such as pea protein, spirulina, kelp powder, and dulse powder. When I include this protein powder in my morning smoothie, its flavor does not overshadow the taste of the fruits and vegetables in the smoothie.
3. The predominant protein in this product is pea protein, and secondarily hemp protein. The manufacturer has done a good job disguising the taste of the pea protein because, on its own, pea protein tastes awful.
4. Surprisingly, the product description on Amazon for this product does not trumpet the fact that it includes Sacha Inchi, chia seeds, spirulina, kelp powder, or dulse powder. That’s actually a positive, because it is clear from the product label that the amount of these ingredients that is included in this protein powder is clearly minimal. According to the FDA, food manufacturers are required to list all ingredients in the food on the label, and "they are to be listed in order of predominance, with the ingredients used in the greatest amount first, followed in descending order by those in smaller amounts." Since Sacha Inchi protein is listed fourth, after the cocoa powder that is merely used as flavoring, I would assume there is not enough of it in this product to offer any of the much vaunted health benefits of this food product (see below for more information on Sacha Inchi). Likewise for the chia seed, spirulina, kelp powder, and dulse powder. Since the chia is listed after natural flavor, and the spirulina, kelp, and dulse are listed dead last on the product label, below salt—which one would hope is in absolutely minimal amounts since there is no reason for it to be in the product at all—there is no need to consider these ingredients whatsoever in making a decision about the potential health benefits of this product.
5. The price of this product is not cheap, but it is in line with what most other vegan protein powders cost these days.

CONS

1. Only one ingredient is organic, the hemp protein.
2. This protein powder comes in a container made of thick plastic. Regardless of the claim of the plastic being a recyclable type, less than 9% of plastic generated in the US is actually recycled. There is no good reason why this product could not be packaged in a biodegradable, resealable Kraft bag instead of a plastic container.

INFORMATION ON SACHA INCHI

Nutritional Information: 1 ounce of these seeds contains over 8 grams of protein and almost 3 grams of fiber. The fat they contain is unsaturated. They contain phosphorus, potassium, magnesium, calcium, and zinc, as well as various antioxidants.

Sacha Inchi has recently become popular as one of the latest in a long line of health food products labeled as "superfoods." The botanical name is Plukenetia volubilis. It is a perennial plant native to South America and the Caribbean. Like the pomegranate fruit, it is known for its large, edible seeds. It has been traditionally consumed by indigenous groups in Peru and, for that reason, it is sometimes called the mountain peanut or Inca nut. The seeds are traditionally roasted, rather than eaten raw, which is a fortunate thing. When raw, these seeds contain antinutrients and alkaloids. (Antinutrients hinder the absorption of micronutrients in the body, and alkaloids are protective agents within plants that defend them against attacks from predators. When consumed in very large amounts, either of these substances can be harmful to the health.)

The roasted seeds can be either eaten whole or ground into a fine powder, such as what is contained in this product. The oil of these seeds is also frequently extracted and utilized in food products or skin care products. The leaves of the Sacha Inchi plant are also dried and brewed into an herbal tea.

review_text:
Okay first off, got to comment this does not state how many come in the pack, you get 24 bars, 8 of each. This should be on the product information, it isn't. It's not overly minty, but just enough to really enjoy it with that icing and chocolate flavor. It builds almost. I really like it alot.

For a little over 2$ a bar, can I recommend it? Uh...50$ is alot. But 24 bars is a decent amount too, so I'm not sure. I would say if it were just cookies and cream, and the mint, yes. Adding caramel, I would say that flavor just brings it down, but if you want protein bars that's something. I don't need protein bars, but if I did I wouldn't turn any of these down. As it stands for me now, they're a meal supplement bar, even if they're not really equipped to be a great option.

So I would say, yes I recommend it, but I would see about buying those other two flavors individually. Also I can't endorse paying for a product that I don't know exactly how much of it I'm getting, which is why I made such a point to state about that first.

review_title: WOW... A-cid WOW! These are Great!
review_text:
Let's start this with a little science, in case you were wondering: What is the difference between BCAAs and EAA? After all, I have been in the workout supplement world for 12 years now and tried a whole lot of different products, but most of the time you only ever hear about BCAAs. To make a long story short, BCAA is 3 of the 9 essential Amino Acids your body cannot make on its own. Thats right, without a supplement for them, you are very unlikely to get the proper amount after a workout. EAAs (such as this product) contain, not only BCAAs (valine, leucine, and isoleucine) but also the other 6 (histidine, lysine, phenylalanine, threonine, methionine, and tryptophan) you don't get in BCAA specific products.

So what does this mean to you? This means this product is comprehensive, you get everything in one package! No need to take different supplements to make sure you get all the different aminos you need, they're all here!

So anyway, how does it taste? I ordered the sour gummy worm which tastes extremely similar to the "Beyond Raw" pre workout: "Lit" sour gummy worm flavor (if you've ever had that). If you aren't familiar with that, I'd say it's similar to a lemonade taste, but very well done. You don't have to "choke" it down in order to drink it. The flavor is quite enjoyable.

Mixability: it mixes alright. I'll disclose I used a spoon to do it which is never going to get the best mixability result, but it is not chalky or anything of that sort. I had to stir a couple times while drinking to make sure it didn't coagulate again (but I am certain this was due to not using a shaker cup). This is all to say: it does not mix as easily as the Optimal Nutrition BCAA's, but it does mix well, I was not upset by its mixing properties.

Also, it is Good Manufacturing Product (GMP) certified, which is something you always want to see with a supplement product. Overall, I would say give this product a try! I really enjoy it and I'm sure you will too.

review_text:
We are Hans and Franz, and we are here to review the Huge Supplements Wrecked Pre-Workout Powder! We must say, we are not impressed by the name of this product. Wrecked? What is this, a demolition derby? We are here to pump clap you up, not to wreck you!

Now, let's take a look at the ingredients. We see that it contains L-Citrulline, Beta-Alanine, Hydromax, and L-Tyrosine. These are all ingredients commonly found in pre-workout supplements and are known for their potential ability to increase energy, focus, and endurance. We have to give credit where credit is due, that is a solid list of ingredients.

We also appreciate that the label states that there are "no useless fillers." As you may know, some pre-workout supplements contain a lot of filler ingredients that do not actually provide any benefit, so it is nice to see a product that claims to not contain any of these.

However, we must take issue with the serving size. 30g+ per serving? That seems like an awful lot of powder to consume in one go. It is important to follow the recommended serving size to avoid potential negative side effects. We also wonder if this product is too potent for beginners or those with lower caffeine tolerance.

I don't know about you, but I generally try to avoid it in my own foods and definitely and pet food, because it gives my family and my pets gas, which to me shows that it just doesn't digest very well and isn't really meant to be a food product.

True to form, this did provide some mild stomach upset, but thankfully there wasn't enough of it for any major discomfort. However, the other ingredients really made up for the pea protein in here. The herbs and mushrooms in here gave me an incredible boost of energy midday to where I didn't feel like I wanted a nap in the middle of the afternoon and got through my entire day feeling capable to handle everything that was thrown at me. Usually I feel like I need to crash a little before my family is ready for bedtime, but the adaptogens and mushrooms in here really carried me through. I have tried two different flavors of this, the peanut butter, and the chocolate, and both of them have a good flavor and have the same general ingredient profile. Over the last five days, I've enjoyed this on for days, and have been really impressed with how notable of a difference it makes and how I feel. This would get five stars if they would replace the pea protein with a higher quality protein such as grass fed whey or collagen.

review_text:
Mixed reviews, but I decided to give them a try anyway because I like Orgain products, AND it was on sale, bringing it closer to $1 per bar. I bought the S'mores, and I find them incredible. I expected a strong protein taste, and at first I thought I was picking them up. I tend to chomp on these through my work day, so I take a bite then set aside for awhile, then return to it as needed. I work a physical job and so it isn't easy to just eat a meal. I also need something that can stick to my ribs. I was really pleasantly surprised that I could eat just this and get through my day. I think I had an apple (cut up for same ease of munching) along side it. It wasn't a fluke, because i did it again the next work day, and had same results. So the protein used is a long burner. Coffee, orgain bar, sliced up apple. All good. All day.

Taste? good. Not too sweet
Texture? awesome. Has a good chew. If warm (like sitting in car) it gets a little goey, but it stays solid- no mess. I like the bits of chocolate. Adds good mouth feel.

I'm a big fan of loading up my purse with snack bars-- again, I work a physical job with no real breaks. I like knowing I have something to nibble on as need be. I would also grab for this when I want something candy bar like, and not worry about taking the sugar hit. I just find it all around pleasant, and will likely buy it again (though preferably on sale), and likely try other flavors.

review_title: Very solid protein powder for maintenance
review_text:
I use this about six times a week, one scoop per day in ~12oz water, along with the typical 5g of Creatine and 5g of fiber. I use an electric milk foamer to integrate the powder (avoids clumps of powder sticking to roof/mouth of shaker cup), then shake it in a shaker cup to fully emulsify. This produces a nice, even consistency a little less thick than a vanilla shake.

Flavor-wise - inoffensive. A little protein bitterness but really not much at all, not too sweet, not too creamy. Better than most of the sugary brands out there. No aftertaste. Clean the cup well, though, because this is the kind of powder that will leave an odor if your aren't reasonably thorough.

Comfort-wise - no discomfort if you take it after your sets. No gastrointestinal distress of any sort, no bloating. Decently filling on its own, and quite acceptable with the fiber.

Effect-wise - well I'm plateaued at 183 and have been for a couple years - this didn't change that at all. But it maintained well and isn't to calorie-heavy, so no complaints I suppose.

Cost-wise - worth the price for what you get. Doesn't have the same protein/dollar ratio you can get with some brands, but the flavor's better, which for someone like me, who is content to maintain mass and support the sets, it's fine.

Give it a try if you haven't already, but otherwise unremarkable.

review_title: Delicious and energizing but they could sure skip the pea protein
review_text:
Some years back, nobody had ever heard of pea protein, and now suddenly it is the vegan protein powder all over everything, taking the place of higher quality proteins like grass fed whey or collagen. I think it must be very cheap to manufacture given how prevalent it has become and everything. I don't know about you, but I generally try to avoid it in my own foods and definitely and pet food, because it gives my family and my pets gas, which to me shows that it just doesn't digest very well and isn't really meant to be a food product.

True to form, this did provide some mild stomach upset, but thankfully there wasn't enough of it for any major discomfort. However, the other ingredients really made up for the pea protein in here. The herbs and mushrooms in here gave me an incredible boost of energy midday to where I didn't feel like I wanted a nap in the middle of the afternoon and got through my entire day feeling capable to handle everything that was thrown at me. Usually I feel like I need to crash a little before my family is ready for bedtime, but the adaptogens and mushrooms in here really carried me through. I have tried two different flavors of this, the peanut butter, and the chocolate, and both of them have a good flavor and have the same general ingredient profile. Over the last five days, I've enjoyed this on for days, and have been really impressed with how notable of a difference it makes and how I feel. I guess I can forgive them for the pea protein when they've developed such a good blend of other ingredients.

This would get five stars if they would replace the pea protein with a higher quality protein such as grass fed whey or collagen.

review_title: 27,770% of your daily recommended B12 value!
review_text:
I'm always looking for new ways to spice up my protein drink in the morning. One element of the shake is creatine, and at 1.7g per serving I figured this would be fine.

Then I looked at the rest of the ingredients. This is meant to be a pre-workout drink with ingredients to match, fun things like Shizandra Extract , Yerba Mate, and Goji Berry. They all do the same things, improve energy and reduce fatigue. These ingredients are all unregulated so I take them with a grain of salt (just kidding, there's no sodium in this!). Nothing earth-shattering or different from the usual blends.

Until I reached B12.

How much B12 do you really need? The May Clinic recommends 2.4 micrograms. MICROGRAMS, not milligrams, and not grams. It's not much. Here's what Healthline has to say about it:

"Although B12 supplements are commonly taken to boost energy levels, there is currently no evidence suggesting that more B12 increases energy in people with adequate levels of this vitamin."

This powder contains 1,670 mcg. That translates to 27,770% of your daily recommended value. Let me spell that out for those in the back. This powder contains TWENTY SEVEN THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED AND SEVENTY PERCENT OF THE DAILY RECOMMENDED B12 VALUE.

2,000 mcg is the upper limit for folks who have a deficiency. Unless you have a specific health problem, people like you and I do not need this much. Very few people need this much. It's too much. Way too much. And you're paying for it.

Is this going to harm you? Probably not. But when I see massive doses like this, it's a red flag that someone is throwing massive doses of vitamin at a problem that doesn't necessarily exist, or at least doesn't require such a drastic amount.

And if you feel like your skin is crawling after this, the TWENTY SEVEN THOUSAND PERCENT of the daily recommended value just might be why!

review_title: coffee smoothie, nice for an afternoon pick me up, good assortment of ingredients, worth trying
review_text:
I have tried the Iconic Immunity coffee in Mocha, Vanilla, and Dark coffee options. Of the three I like the Dark Roast best, followed by Chocolate (surprises me since I dont like chocolate as much as vanilla in general), then vanilla. Of the three, this dark roast has a little more coffee taste come through, but it also has a little more protein taste or something that comes through. It isn't bad, it just needs to be very cold. When over ice, it is quite pleasant. But I can also drink it room temp, too.

So while not incredible, it is totally drinkable. It is something that would likely appeal most to those on the go, or who dont want to/or have time for making their own coffee smoothie. Great for those that are traveling. While I prefer it ice cold, it is fine at room temp. Drink on its own or use as base for other smoothie ingredients. Very well packaged and secured.

Has a creamy taste and mouth feel, yet is non dairy. No other flavors really stand out--yet there is something else there peeking around the corner, I just cant pin point it. Overall, just a mild, easy to drink vanilla flavor. This doesn't have that brutally stark protein flavor that can come through on drinks of this nature-- at least to me.

I think the nutrition profile is overall solid and which is the primary factor that goes into my rating. Are the nutrients/ingredients worthwhile? How does the info on bottle compare to what is listed on product page? Then I factor in my perception of taste (subjective, but still informative). Bascially anything I can think of that may help a would be buyer make a decision. I dont know your budget, so I only comment on price (not directly rate).

And so, I think this has a little bit of everything, including fiber. 80 calories, sweetened with both monk fruit extract AND stevia. A little high on sodium for the 8 ounce container, but I like the low cals, and the addition of fiber, protein, zinc,& vitamin D3, vitamin C, MCT oil. 200mg caffeine.

Really a nice mid morning, early afternoon pick me up. I drink a cup of coffee very early in the morning while I take care of my dogs and cats, watch some news, etc. Then I make a big smoothie that I consume some of before doing a work out. Then I take off with remainder of my smoothie for a busy day of an active job. I normally have a want for something- somewhere between 11a-1p. THIS has been coming in handy. It's pricy even for me, but it has been a very welcome addition. Take my money? lol

I dont rate on price (we all have our own budgets, values), but this is a bit prohibitive to me at $3.49 per bottle. I would expect this to be no more than that for a ingle bottle in a drug store, but not as a multi pack. Again, I dont factor this into my rating unless its offered as a "rate features" option. I like it, I think it may be worth the try. It isn't dessert, but it isn't off putting. It is more protein drink tasting than coffee, but it works like coffee (plus other goodies)

review_title: Works fairly well but sometimes struggles to mix everything
review_text:
This is a fun twist on the typical shaker bottle. It's basically a low-powered wireless blender. The lights that come on on the base unit when it's spinning are fun and help to see how mixed your drink is.

The charge seems to last quite a while and I'm a big fan of the fact that the charging port is a magnet that can easily come disconnected if the cord gets caught on something.

The blending ability of the bottle is functional but not perfect. There have been a number of times where I've tried to mix protein powder into water in this and a small amount of the powder gets stuck to the side of the bottle without dissolving, even when running the "blender" portion of the bottle multiple times. I was able to shake the bottle a bit and get everything to mix in but that defeats the point of the bottle.

Adding soap and water to the bottle and spinning it up only works to clean the bottle if you do it immediately after making and drinking a protein shake, otherwise it does not have the power to clean the dried residue off the sides of the bottle. This isn't a huge issue though sine the bottle is dishwasher safe which I'm a big fan of.

The seal on the lid and flip-up portion are good, I've had no issues with leakage. I did find the mouth opening to be slightly smaller than normal, but it's still completely functional.

All in all, this is a solid option if you can't or don't want to use a shaker cup that you have to shake yourself, or if you just want to add some fun to making protein shakes. It mixes fairly well and doesn't leave chunks, but sometimes powder does get stuck to the side of the bottle.

product_title: Kaged Muscle Clean Meal; Meal Replacement Shake with Whey Protein Isolate, Clean Carbs, MCT Oil Fats, Organic Vitamins and Minerals, Snickerdoodle, 20 Servings
review_text:
This is a great MEAL replacement powder. Note the emphasis on: meal; it is not a pure protein powder. Although it contains plenty of protein, it also contains many of the other ingredients that you would expect from a meal, such as (healthy) fats, some carbohydrates (from oat flour and quinoa), and a multivitamin blend. Unless you are on a strict ketogenic diet, you do not have to be afraid of this small amount of carbs. Kaged provides a well-balanced meal that nicely (and deliciously) serves its purpose.

Regrettably, this site does not show the Food Label, which is a pity, because the list of contents is very good. On my tub (vanilla cake), it states: 2 Scoops (59 g): Total Fat: 4.5 g; Cholesterol: 0 mg; Sodium: 45 mg; Total Carbohydrate: 18 g; Dietary Fiber: 2 g; Total Sugars: 1 g; Protein: 28 g. It also contains sucralose, which for some people might be a no-go, despite the otherwise well-selected ingredients. The fiber content could be higher (healthier), especially since this is intended as a meal that is supposed to keep you full for a while. Kaged, if you are listening: add more fiber.

I like the flavor a lot, but realize that people have different taste preferences. It doesn't taste like your typical vanilla shake; rather more like vanilla-nut (perhaps the nutty infusion part is what some reviewers note as "aftertaste"). They should call the flavor "vanilla nut cake". I always use the blender and mix with water or milk (+ 2 ice cubes). It comes out frothy with foam (more so with milk), so I let it settle for a minute or two before drinking (I don’t like to drink foam); maybe this helps to minimize gastrointestinal issues (?), which I don’t have with this product.

Unlike the great variety of offerings in pure protein powders, there are not many true “meal replacement” products out there. But there is a similar one called Eat Right MRP, which is a bit lower in the carb fraction (from potato starch and maltodextrin) and higher in fiber. It has a bit more protein, fats, cholesterol, and sodium; and contains sucralose as well, but overall is rather similar.

Like the Caged product, Eat Right comes in vanilla, which tastes like the typical vanilla cream and is delicious (at least for me; again: every person is different). Eat Right does not foam quite as much, and blended with milk becomes a tad creamy. For variety’s sake, I am alternating between these two delicious MRPs and I’m happy with both, despite minor shortcomings here and there.

review_title: Hemp powder is a great vegan protein source!
review_text: Although I don't follow a vegan diet, my GI system doesn't do too well on whey protein.  I've been using hemp in my daily smoothies to get some extra protein for awhile now.  Hemp protein powder is a complete protein and is up to 98% digestible when cold processed, which is what this product is.  I started with the powdered hemp protein (different brand), then switched to hemp hearts which is shelled hemp seeds.  I liked them better because the powder is more messy.  Didn't really think about a difference in flavor.  Did a little research and discovered that perhaps I shouldn't have switched to the seeds after all!  Comparing 3 Tb of each: The powder contains MORE protein, 18g vs 10g in the seeds.  Powder also contains LESS fat, 6g vs 15g in the seeds. The powder also has MORE fiber, 6g vs 1g in the seeds.  So those are some big differences.  Although I prefer the seeds due to a little less mess and a milder taste, I think I will be switching back to powder.  Gave this brand of powder a try and it seemed a little stronger in flavor than I have been used to for awhile.  Not bad at all, just stronger than the seeds.  I don't remember the color of the powder I used before but this is quite green which I like because I need the chlorophyll.  Note that the package says refrigeration not required, store in a cool, dark, and dry place.  Online it said that to prevent the fats from going rancid it should be stored in the fridge.  Usually you follow package directions so it's up to you.  I am so much healthier now that I am getting more protein in my diet.  This powder helps make that possible!

review_text:
+ Tastes Really Good
+ Whey Isolate is listed before Whey Concentrate on Ingredients list
+ Super cheap
- Not full disclosure label
- Unknown amount of Peptides is concerning

Good replacement for more expensive whey proteins. It is mostly a whey isolate blend, so it should be a large percentage protein. Probably one of the best vanilla flavors as well.

Anytime I see an ingredient blend with supplements, It is a major red flag for me. In this case, we have an unknown amount of peptides mixed with isolate and unknown amount of Whey Concentrate. At least the concentrate is less than the Isolate blend. However peptides are shortened amino strings, meaning they don't need to contain the same amount of amino's as protein. I am concerned they could spike the Isolate/ Peptide blend with cheap, incomplete amino strings. In theory the peptide blend could be (99% amino / 1% isolate). The blend would still get labeled first even though Isolate is the smallest ingredient.

That is a lot of "ifs" and I am not an expert on this matter. So take all that concern as you will. This protein is still cheap and tastes good, for me it is worth the risk.

review_text:
Overall, I like it. It has an easy to drink taste: a little sweet, and has a pleasant chocolate flavor. Not strong. Tastes fine on its own, or pairs nicely with other add-ins. Light on calories and the serving is 1 scoop, which is large. Use more if need be. 21 serving sized bag. At $26.89, that makes it $1.28 per serving. I dont rate on price, you will have to decide if that is a good price to you or not. I'll happily use this up, but not sure yet if it is a repurchase.

I used to often buy Vivanno from Starbuckss which used a chocolate protein powder, banana, and coffee. That hasn't been around in forever, and so I make them at home as a pick-me-up Using dried instant), or as a meal replacement if I have a meal replacement powder.

This meal replacement powder is quite low in calories (120 calorie "meal"). So more in line with weight loss through fasting than just replacing a masticating meal/making a liquid meal for other reasons. I find the calories to be lower than some of my meal replacement powders (180-480, which I normally aim for around the 200 mark as I have other add-ins that bump the calories to a wholesome 300-400 cals). I think the overall formula looks good. It could be consumed a few times a day (either larger portion or as meal replacement and/or snack) and not have a concern with vitamin & mineral amounts. Sodium is fair. I have had some pushing 400 mg per serving, and this is moderate at 220 mg per serving.

18 mg of protein is more than plenty for me. Can easily boost it by adding in additional protein powder or collagen powder.

Taste is sweet, with a light chocolate taste. Malty in a pleasant way. If you want a stronger chocolate flavor, add in about TBS of unsweetened chocolate/cocao or cacoa powder (like hershey brand for baking)-- very low calories (10) with loads of nutrients.

How I use meal replacement shakes: I tend to not eat in the morning. I have my coffee, and usually have no appetite until noon or so. But, some days I want something but I still dont want to eat.. so I drink! Usually a portion of meal replacement powder with non dairy creamer, and sometimes a banana added into mix. I also want my vitamins and minerals, so I choose a meal replacement powder instead of a plain protein powder (sometimes the proteins powders just have too much protein, and it bothers my gut). Sometimes I incorporate other add-ins (usually other powder supplements- mushroom, adaptogens, collagen, matcha--goes well with vanilla powders). That will all keep me going until dinner. Or I will have it along side a light meal. Keeps me energized.

I did try this out initially just prepared with some non dairy milk. 8 ounces of liquid with 120 calories does not make a meal. I was feeling ravenous shortly after, almost better if I hadnt eaten anything. A little more fiber (3 grams as prepared) would make this better in terms of controlling hunger. Maybe add in your own fiber (whole food blended into a smoothie, or on the side) to get a few more calories and belly filling fiber. If I wanted to have something early as a "breakfast" this could work. At least it is something.

I dont like to snack, so I likely wouldnt use this for that. Anything consumed will raise blood glucose levels, which is already problematic but also in terms of weight loss. So no grazing. I eat meals. I just dont need 6 of them, or even 3 of them. Usually just two. Sometimes a complete meal replacement with a shake like this, sometimes along with a small meal. But you do you. If 120 calories can stave off your hunger, then go for it.

The solution foams, which isn't uncommon from protein powders and 25% of the powder remains undisolved after vigorous shaking. I use a wand blender and the results are the same.

You have to make it in advance and allow it to sit for 30min-1hr for the foam to subside and for the remaining powder to dissolve.

I consume a normal milk based (white) whey protein shake for breakfast and throw this in a bottle to consume on my lunch break. By then its fully dissolved.

Citrus Lemonade is tolerable but I've found that using an orange or lemonade "water enhancer" works great. You'll find them on Amazon or in the drink isle of your supermarket.
