review_text:
I've been eating Power Crunch bars on and off for many years. I rely on them when I am cutting back on sugar. These make for an excellent treat if you happen to like the wafer style cookies (or even kitkats). You know.. that style that normally come in vanilla, strawberry, or chocolate. Except these are coated. I would buy a pack, and gobble them all up. Loads of sugar and calories later with no other nutrient value, I would feel a little gross in my belly. So Power Crunch really saves the day. I can use them as a treat, or as a means for boosting protein. I truly enjoy these, and dont just look at them as a consolation prize.

I love vanilla, so this flavor is my favorite. I haven't met a variety I haven't liked, but the vanilla is my jam.

Not too sweet, not too "protein powder" tasting (that can otherwise ruin a good looking healthy snack bar), and I can stop at one. Which is good because they are 220 calories a piece, not that far off from a regular candy bar. BUT, it isnt loaded with sugar (just 5 added sugars, same as a gummy vitamin), and it is a good size. I feel satisfied with one.

The sweetness level is low on these. If you are used to eating lots of sweet things, then this may taste more bland. I find that true of most things when I switch from sugar laden diet to a sugar restricted diet. Takes awhile for taste buds to adjust. So keep that in mind if you are just starting off and are looking for treat alternatives. If you have been cutting sugar, then this is a perfect level of sweet. Just enough to be tasty, yet not enough to be cloying. LOVE IT SO MUCH

I would love to see the bar made into two sticks, or two squares.

If you are like me, though, it's a pros and cons thing. Unless you have serious gut lining issues, I'd tend to say it's not worth it. review_text:
So why 4 stars instead of 5? I'll start there. The instructions say, serving size 1 scoop, 30g. So I made the shake using that serving. It seemed light on powder. The container says 20 servings, and it seemed like there's more than that based on the scoop. So I weighed the scoop. It's a 15g scoop that's included. So they've got bad serving information on the bottle.

Next, calling it pea protein isn't attractive, then you realize it's yellow pea. That's getting worse. I of course got the double chocolate yellow pea powder. I'm not running out to tell my friends and family that.

So how's the product?

The first smell after opening it, there was a slight chocolate smell, nothing offensive, that's good.

The initial taste of the powder on my finger, not bad, mild chocolate.

I'll ignore the first 2 days of using it with the wrong serving size. I have a protein shake every morning. It consists of.

8oz milk
1 frozen banana
1 serving protein powder
1 serving peanut butter powder
Topped with ice and water to fill the blender cup

Sounds good, right.

Since I don't ever drink any protein powder using the just add water or milk recipe, I test using my recipe.

Ok, this tasted pretty good. The chocolate flavor was light, and as a result the sweetener from the stevia was light as well. There was a very nice creamy consistency to my shake, which I was impressed by. It did have that plant based protein shake look of sludge, but I'm used to that now.

I've definitely had protein powders that have a stronger flavor, and I'm not saying that a stronger flavor would be better.

I think you'll find this will not offend you. You'll also find that it won't wow you. It's a good quality double chocolate yellow pea powder.

I'll continue to drink this, using the correct serving size. I think drinking more of this might make some other brands taste weird, because I can see getting used to this subtle flavor over time.

So, ultimately, I would say this is good protein powder, I'd recommend it. Just make sure you know the correct serving size. This isn't super concentrated, so a small scooper means two scoops of double chocolate yellow pea powder.

I hope you found this review helpful.

review_text:
So I have mixed the minimum mix, (there are three concentrations 2, 4, or 6 scoops in 8 oz of water,) and the result is a somewhat syrupy drink I can barely tolerate. The mixed fruit flavor tastes pretty intense and this was at the lowest concentration. Then I feel strange. Of course I cannot exactly describe this but feeling like you had a stroke may get the closest. Things are not right but there is no pain in your head either. Considering the reaction though I am a little dismayed.

I used to mix this with other protein powders, fruit, and vegetable powders but I stopped doing that and wanted to just get a pick me up of energy. This does not work that way for me. This may just be how my body reacts to it. They sell a lot of it so this is solely my experience. Also, I do not recommend getting it on auto delivery as I now have two of these and I don't want to use them. My friend wanted to try the drink but her results were not good either. This energy drink must have reacted with her anti depressant and she felt frighteningly terrible (without going into detail.)

So this is a classic caveat emptor. If it works for you then great. If it does not work then be prepared to return it before the return window closes. Since these supplements are not classified as food or drugs there is really very little regulation or oversight. (It seems to me that everything should be one or the other if you consume it.) So your mileage may vary. And if you can tolerate the flavor... this may be just the thing you want. Bon chance.

I've read that some people experience improvement with joint pain on collagen, but my arthritis is inflammatory and so is not affected by collagen. I've been on Zhou Collagen Peptides for three months now, and I've noticed some baby hairs around my hairline. *IT'S IMPORTANT TO NOTE HERE I AM ALSO TAKING ZHOU HAIRFLUENCE VITAMINS* The results I see in my hair, skin, and nails is subtle and gradual, but it's a definite difference. I've noticed that the little "jowlets" (acquired after developing a prednisone moon face overnight, maintaining it for six years, then losing it over a couple of weeks) are annoying me less and less. Are they shrinking? Is my skin just glowing so much I don't notice them? I can't say exactly. But I was obsessed with how much I hate them, and now I don't even notice them most of the time. And I feel like my marionette line (acquired by pain scowling every day for years) are softening, just a little. These things are important to me because I am waaaay to young to have marionette lines and jowls. And I hate being reminded of how badly I feel every time I look in the mirror. I really do think the collagen is helping, combined with the best diet I can manage, lots and lots of water, and daily sunscreen.

Just to be clear, I paid for each cannister of Zhou Collagen Peptides with my own money and have not been compensated for my review in any way.

review_text:
I am used to consuming hydrolyzed collagen powder. I have been buying it for years and I love how many different options and flavors have come out over time. I tend to buy plain (so versatile), vanilla, or chocolate- the later great for adding into smoothies or "coffee elixirs" as I call my hot coffee blended beverage with nourishing add-ins. But pink lemonade? Sure, why not?! Especially on a hot humid day.. a cup of cold lemonade sounds great.

I take a 16 ounce mason jar (I use them as regular glasses), add 2 scoops of this powder, fill the cup 3/4 of the way with cold water- stir vigorously-- add a bunch of ice cubes, top rest of way with more water if need be. This makes for a refreshing, slightly sweet, semi tart ice cold summer beverage that also happens to provide some protein, collagen peptides, and vitamin C. TThe taste has a sweet-tart thing going on except not a cloying sweet. It doesn't lean too lemony, so take them up on their suggestion to add a squeeze of lemon juice. Sometimes I add a splash of lemon (or lime) juice to amp up the citrus flavor, sometimes I add a small pour of tart cherry juice concentrate or pomegranate juice concentrate. Sometimes nothing extra at all-- I like it as is too. OOh one more option, is adding a scoop (or two) to a large bottle of water. Clearly the water to product ratio will determine how much flavor comes through. For those days you don't want plain water and don't need a lot of flavor, add some of this to a big bottle of water for a hint of flavor.

It is a fun, refreshing way to have a dose of collagen without it being in a typical smoothie. Now I know I could take plain collagen peptides and add it to a lemon drink, but I really just like this. I wont buy it all year, but I do like it during these hot days. It just has a summery vibe to it.

Love the addition of vitamin C as that boosts the collagen absorption.

If the flavor sounds good, and the price seems right to you.. then I would give it a try. I am really enjoying it right now.

Drinking it on its own is rather unpleasant.

This protein powder you need a blender bottle or blender for it. You cannot stir it into a drink since it will not dissolve. This will ruin a cup of coffee. This would ruin the taste of most drinks you add it to.

Protein powder is usually inexpensive. The current cost of $44.85 for seven servings, which is $6.41 per serving, does not make sense. You can get pea protein, cacao powder, chia seeds, etc., for much less money. There is no real benefit to combining all these ingredients into one powder unless you really want all these ingredients. Chia seeds are best ground right before eating to preserve freshness.

The drink does not look like the marketing photos. The marketing photos appear to have artificial chocolate syrup added in.

review_title: Good flavor, quite clean, huge bag, I'm a fan
review_text:
I've tried a lot of different protein products and I'm quite pleased by this one.

The flavor is good, not amazing but definitely still good. It differs from a lot of the "chocolate" flavored protein powders that I've had in that this one almost reminds me of dark chocolate. Honestly, it's a nice change of pace from the stereotypical chocolate flavors that are everywhere these days.

The bag is pretty big, as would be expected with a 10 lb bag, and as a result the price tag might be a bit daunting. Each serving (one scoop) contains 25g of protein and there are approximately 137.5 servings in the bag for a total of 3440g of protein for $125 or 27.5g of protein per dollar. That's pretty competitive compared to other brands. It's not the cheapest out there, but it's a very reasonable price.

The ingredients look good as well, which surprises me given the reasonable price. One of the first things I like to look at when trying a new protein powder is the number of ingredients that are in it. It's usually a red flag when there's a huge number of ingredients added into the mix. Fortunately, this powder has very few added ingredients on top of the protein, which is one of the things they advertise ("7 simple ingredients") that I'm a fan of. Of the 120 calories per serving, 100 calories are from protein and the other 20 are from fat and carbs (including 1g of sugar which to me is negligible).

In terms of the protein itself, it's a mix of whey isolate and whey concentrate (with more isolate than concentrate based on the order listed in the ingredients list). I generally prefer isolate-only protein powders and I dislike the fact that it's unknown how much of each is actually in this product, but the fact that there's only 20 calories coming from fat/carbs tells me there's not a ton of whey concentrate.

All-in-all, this is a great protein product that gives you clean ingredients for a very reasonable price, plus the added convenience of not needing to buy as often since the bag is so big. I would definitely recommend this!

review_text:
Like other reviewers with a less than positive experience, it pains me to write this review because I love Kelly, have all of her books, and follow her nutritional advice with great results. Sadly, this powder really did not work for me. I do believe in the quality and ethical sourcing of the ingredients used, so stars for that.

The packaging, while more eco friendly than a plastic container, is a NIGHTMARE to work with. You have to dig your hand so far down to get to the scooper and end up covered in sticky collagen powder (and also wasting product). I have tried mixing the product into smoothies, using a hand mixer, hot water, coffee, almond milk in my Nespresso frother (hot and cold setting), and 90% of the time this stuff just DOES. NOT. MIX. It clumps no matter how little or how slowly you add it. I really tried to make it work but it was near impossible to get it to mix into anything and if it did, it ended up settling on the bottom of my glass before I was finished.

I also experienced the crazy frothiness of the product the few times I was actually able to get it to incorporate, but I was using it in a latte so it really didn't bother me much. I didn't experience any GI issues from this product as others did. I ordered both the original and vanilla and while I don't get any beef taste from either, the vanilla is sickeningly sweet and has a horrible aftertaste. I tried mixing the unflavored and vanilla to try and mellow the sweetness but it is just so overpowering.

Again, I feel horrible writing this review but this product is expensive and I wouldn't want someone to spend their hard earned money on a product that is unsatisfactory. Will stick with my trusted brands of collagen/protein for my Fab4 needs.

review_title: Middle of the road powder, flavor okay
review_text:
I'm slowly working my way through every single protein powder on Amazon that's sold in 4lb tubs or greater. This one is a middle-of-the-road powder. Not offensively sweet, which is nice - there may be a vague hint of the "ice cream" part of "chocolate ice cream", but not much. It has a protein-chocolate flavor - the powders with a higher protein content tend to have that typical bitter flavor profile - but it isn't too noticeable. Decent consistency, sort of creamy, which I like. Mixes well, especially if you let it sit for ~15m, but not the thickest powder I've had. No gastro issues that I can tell, at least so far.

So it's okay. I only use powder for maintenance, not bulking, and this seems up to the task. I have no particular reason to order this powder again over any other, but if you are just getting started on protein, this will do fine.
